definition_zh: 物种；种类；（法律）形式；类型
definition_en: a group of living things that share characteristics and can breed with each other, or a kind or type of something

scene: 博物馆的标本柜排成长长一列，讲解员轻轻拉开一只抽屉。This drawer holds a bird species found only on that remote island.
sceneCN: 这里 species 是「物种」（第 1 个义项：能互相繁育的一类生物）；句意为这个抽屉装着只在那座偏远岛屿上发现的鸟类物种。图中可辨识物件：标本柜、抽屉、鸟类标本。

senses.title: A group of breeding organisms
senses.titleCN: 物种：能互相繁育的一类生物
senses.definition: a group of living organisms that resemble one another and can interbreed to produce fertile young
senses.definitionCN: 彼此相似、能互相交配繁殖出可育后代的一类生物
senses.example: This frog species exists only in the mountain streams of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这种青蛙只存在于那座岛的山间溪流中。
senses.why: Latin species meant an appearance or a kind; biologists fixed the word to the natural kind that keeps breeding true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 species 本指「外貌、种类」；生物学家把这个固定在能稳定繁衍后代的那一类自然生命上。

senses.title: A kind or type of thing
senses.definition: a kind, sort, or variety of something, especially when it is one among many
senses.definitionCN: 某物的种类、类别或样式，尤指众多之中的一类
senses.example: The shop sells many species of cactus from dry deserts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店售卖许多来自干旱沙漠的仙人掌种类。
senses.why: The classifying image extends beyond life: anything that can be sorted into a kind can be called a species.
senses.whyCN: 分类的意象延伸到生命之外：凡能归入一类的都可称一种 species。

senses.title: Human beings as a kind
senses.definition: the human species, considered as one biological kind among others
senses.definitionCN: 把人类当作生物中的一种来看待
senses.example: The human species has changed the climate of the whole planet.
senses.exampleCN: 人类这一物种改变了整个星球的气候。
senses.why: People themselves form one of the kinds in the great cabinet of living things.
senses.whyCN: 人类本身就是生命大柜中的一格。

senses.title: The outward appearance or form
senses.definition: the visible form or appearance of something, especially in legal or philosophical language
senses.definitionCN: 事物的外在形式或样貌，多见于法律或哲学术语
senses.example: In old legal texts, species referred to the exact form of the property.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧法律文本中，species 指财产的确切形式。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, close to the Latin root: what shows itself to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，贴近拉丁词根：呈现在眼前的样子。

senses.title: In chemistry: a distinct form
senses.titleCN: 化学物种：一种确定的形态
senses.definition: a distinct kind of atom, molecule, or ion present in a substance or reaction
senses.definitionCN: 物质或反应中存在的某种确定的原子、分子或离子形态
senses.example: The reaction produces several charged species in the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 该反应在溶液中产生几种带电的化学物种。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the sorting image: each distinct molecular kind is a species of its own.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了分类意象：每种确定的分子形态自成一个 species。

senses.title: A specific variety within a genus
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank below genus in the classification of living things
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中低于「属」的一个层级
senses.example: The genus roses contains over one hundred species.
senses.exampleCN: 蔷薇属包含一百多个物种。
senses.why: In the ladder of classification, species is the rung directly under genus.
senses.whyCN: 在分类的阶梯上，物种是紧挨「属」下面的一级。

senses.title: Companion species: coexistence
senses.definition: a species that lives alongside another and depends on or affects it
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物种共同生活、依赖或影响它的物种
senses.example: Ants are companion species for many flowering plants.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁是许多开花植物的伴生物种。
senses.why: Kinds do not live alone: each kind is defined partly by the company it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 物种不是孤立生活的：每个物种的定义部分取决于它所相伴的对象。

senses.title: Endangered species as a category
senses.titleCN: 濒危物种：受威胁的一类
senses.definition: a species whose numbers have fallen so far that it may disappear
senses.definitionCN: 数量已下降到可能消失程度的一类生物
senses.example: The panda was long listed as an endangered species.
senses.exampleCN: 大熊猫长期被列为濒危物种。
senses.why: The cabinet drawer can close forever: a kind that dies out is a kind lost.
senses.whyCN: 柜子的抽屉可能永远合上：灭绝的一类就是永远失去的一类。

intro.en: Species comes from Latin through frequent philosophical and scientific use, and its whole story is about seeing and sorting.
intro.cn: species 来自拉丁语，经过哲学与科学的长期使用，整个故事围绕「观看与分类」展开。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as "to observe, look at". The deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察、看」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: In Latin, species meant "appearance, form, a particular kind", from specere "to look at".
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 由 specere「看」派生，意为「外貌、形式、特定的种类」。

items.en: Medieval philosophers used species for the form things impress on the mind, alongside genus.
items.cn: 中世纪哲学家把 species 用于事物印入心灵的形式，与 genus「属」并立。

items.en: The word entered English in the sixteenth century with the senses of kind and outward form.
items.cn: 该词于十六世纪进入英语，带有「种类」与「外在形式」两义。

items.en: Biologists from Ray to Darwin made species the basic unit of classification and evolution.
items.cn: 从雷到达尔文，生物学家把物种确立为分类与进化的基本单位。

items.en: Everyday English uses species both for living kinds and loosely for any sort of thing.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它指生物物种，也泛指任何一类东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same seeing root and similar spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for kinds and sorts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「观看」词根的词与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示种类、类别的词。

entries.definition: A single example taken from a group for study; from the same Latin root specere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标本、样本」，从同一拉丁词根 specere 派生。

entries.definition: A technical verb meaning to form new species in evolution.
entries.definitionCN: 专业动词，义为「形成新物种」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning particular or distinctive; from the same family of Latin words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「特别的、专门的」，来自同一拉丁词族。

entries.definition: Something striking to look at; built on the same seeing root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「景象、奇观」，建立在同一「观看」词根上。

entries.definition: Plural of spice, the kitchen ingredient; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: spice 的复数，指香料；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A general word for a class of similar things; everyday and not biological.
entries.definitionCN: 表示一类相似之物的常用词，日常用语，不带生物学色彩。

entries.definition: The taxonomic rank above species; it groups several species together.
entries.definitionCN: 分类学中高于种的层级，把若干物种归为一组。

entries.definition: A subdivision within a species, or simply a diverse assortment.
entries.definitionCN: 物种内部的细分单元，或泛指多样的种类。

entries.definition: A cultivated variety within an animal species, especially domestic ones.
entries.definitionCN: 动物物种内部培育出的品种，尤指家养动物。

entries.definition: A general class in any system of sorting, not tied to living things.
entries.definitionCN: 任何分类体系中的大类，不限于生物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及该词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: specere is to look: a species is a kind you can point to once you have looked.
normal.cn: specere 意为「看」：物种就是看过之后能明确指出的一类。

normal.en: The same root gives inspect, spectator and respect; all involve looking.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 inspect、spectator、respect，都与「看」有关。

normal.en: An endangered species is a kind on the edge of vanishing.
normal.cn: endangered species 指濒临消失的物种。

normal.en: Biologists define a species by breeding: members can produce fertile young.
normal.cn: 生物学家以繁育定义物种：同种成员能繁殖可育后代。

normal.en: The phrase origin of species names the famous book by Darwin.
normal.cn: origin of species 是达尔文名著《物种起源》的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a long cabinet of drawers: each drawer holds one kind of life, neatly labelled.
abstract.cn: 想象一排抽屉柜：每个抽屉装着一类生命，标签整齐。

abstract.en: Two animals belong in the same drawer when their young can also breed.
abstract.cn: 当两种动物的后代也能繁育时，它们属于同一个抽屉。

abstract.en: A closed drawer forever is an extinct kind: the label remains, the life is gone.
abstract.cn: 永远合上的抽屉就是灭绝的一类：标签还在，生命已逝。

examples.en: Scientists discovered a new species of owl in the rainforest.
examples.cn: 科学家在雨林中发现了一个新的猫头鹰物种。

examples.en: The wetland shelters dozens of bird species every winter.
examples.cn: 这片湿地每年冬天庇护数十种鸟类。

examples.en: Human activity threatens thousands of species with extinction.
examples.cn: 人类活动威胁着数以千计的物种，使其面临灭绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比西兹」——柜子里的标本彼此相似：一类物种

root: 拉丁语 species「外貌、种类」由动词 specere「观看」派生；一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察」，更早来源不确定。同一词根生出 spectare「注视」与希腊语 skopein「看」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of species move from the biological kind outward: sorting any things into kinds, humans as one kind among them, and the fixed ranks of classification.
sensesIntro.cn: species 的义项从生物学物种向外扩展：把万物归为类别、把人类视为其中一类，再到分类学固定层级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled cabinet where each drawer holds one kind of living thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排贴着标签的柜子，每个抽屉装着一类生物。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGY LINE: the kind that breeds true sits at a fixed rung below genus.
branches.cn: 生物学线：能稳定繁育的一类位于「属」下面的固定层级。

branches.en: THE SORTING LINE: any things that resemble each other can be called a kind, humans included.
branches.cn: 归类线：彼此相似的任何事物都可称为一类，人类也在其中。

branches.en: THE OLD FORM LINE: before biology, the word meant the outward appearance itself.
branches.cn: 古义线：在生物学之前，这个词指外在形式本身。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY LINE: each distinct molecular form becomes its own kind.
branches.cn: 化学线：每种确定的分子形态自成一 kind。

branches.en: THE LIVING-TOGETHER LINE: kinds coexist with others, and some now stand at the edge of vanishing.
branches.cn: 共存线：物种与其他物种相伴而生，有些如今濒临消失。

intro.en: Species is a bare Latin noun; English builds on it mostly through the related seeing root.
intro.cn: species 本身是拉丁名词；英语主要通过相关的「观看」词根在其上构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere and its derivatives are well recorded; only the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 及其派生词均有文献记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root appears in spectator and inspect.
items.exampleCN: 该词根出现在 spectator 与 inspect 中。

items.example: The verb is the parent of species.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 species 的来源。

items.example: The noun names what is seen as a kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被看作一类的东西。
它构成 specimen 与 speciation。

items.example: It appears in spectacle and inspect.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 spectacle 与 inspect 中。

definition_zh: 明确的；具体的；特定的；特有的；特效的
definition_en: clearly defined and exact, or relating to one particular thing rather than others
core_image: 放大镜对准一点：众多可能里只锁定那一个
scene: 问卷上的选项太多了，老师指着其中一格。Please give one specific example from your own experience.
sceneCN: 这里 specific 是「具体的、明确的」（第 1 个义项：清楚确定、不笼统的）；句意为请从你自己的经历中举出一个具体的例子。图中可辨识物件：问卷、铅笔、老师的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：明确的；具体的；特定的
名词：细节；特效药（复数 specifics）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「明确性；特异性」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「明确地；特别地」
由同族动词 specify 派生，义为「规格；说明书」

senses.title: Clearly defined and exact
senses.definition: clear and precise, leaving no doubt about what is meant
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、精确，对所指毫无含糊
senses.example: The report gave a specific date for the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 报告给出了发布的确定日期。
senses.why: The magnifying glass drops on one point: out of many possibilities, one is named exactly.
senses.whyCN: 放大镜落在一点上：在众多可能中，只精确指出一个。

senses.title: Particular rather than general
senses.definition: relating to one particular thing, person, or case rather than things in general
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一特定事物、人或情形，而非泛指
senses.example: This medicine targets a specific type of bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药针对特定的一类细菌。
senses.why: The lens can be aimed: whatever it lands on becomes the special one among many.
senses.whyCN: 镜头可以瞄准：它落到哪里，哪里就从众多中成为被选中的那一个。

senses.title: Peculiar to something
senses.definition: found or effective only in connection with one particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 只与某一特定事物相关或对其有效
senses.example: The rash is specific to this tropical region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种皮疹是这一热带地区特有的。
senses.why: What the lens isolates belongs to that thing alone and to nothing else.
senses.whyCN: 镜头所隔离之物只属于那一事物，不属于其他。

senses.title: Detailed and concrete in information
senses.definition: containing details that are concrete and usable, not vague
senses.definitionCN: 包含具体可用的细节，不含糊其辞
senses.example: Her feedback was specific enough to fix the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 她的反馈足够具体，可以据此修改草稿。
senses.why: Precision has degrees: the more the glass magnifies, the more detail shows.
senses.whyCN: 精确有程度：放大越多，细节越多。

senses.title: In medicine: acting on one target
senses.definition: acting effectively against one particular disease or agent and not others
senses.definitionCN: 只对某一特定疾病或病原有效，对其他无效
senses.example: Quinine became a specific treatment for malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 奎宁成为治疗疟疾的特效药。
senses.why: Old pharmacy used the noun specific for a remedy aimed at exactly one ailment.
senses.whyCN: 旧时药房用名词 specific 指专治某一种病的特效药。

senses.title: A precise detail
senses.definition: a precise item of information, usually in the plural specifics
senses.definitionCN: 一条精确的信息，常用复数 specifics
senses.example: The contract still lacks the specifics of payment.
senses.exampleCN: 合同仍缺少付款的具体细节。
senses.why: Turn the adjective into a noun and you hold the magnified details in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 把形容词变成名词，被放大的细节就握在手中。

senses.title: In biology: limited to one species
senses.definition: restricted to or characteristic of one biological species
senses.definitionCN: 仅限于或专属于某一生物物种
senses.example: The virus shows strong species-specific behaviour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒表现出很强的物种特异性。
senses.why: The exactness of the lens becomes biological: it fits one living kind only.
senses.whyCN: 镜头的精确性变成生物学概念：它只匹配一种生物。

senses.title: Made definite by naming
senses.definition: made definite by naming the very thing intended
senses.definitionCN: 通过指明确切对象而变得确定
senses.example: The winner was made specific once the envelope opened.
senses.exampleCN: 信封一开，获奖者就确定了。
senses.why: Naming is the final act of precision: the one thing is finally spoken.
senses.whyCN: 指名是精确的最终动作：那唯一的事物终于被说出。

intro.en: Specific comes from Latin via Late Latin and Old French, and its family is all about naming a kind exactly.
intro.cn: specific 经晚期拉丁语和古法语来自拉丁语，其词族的核心是精确地指明一个种类。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as "to observe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Species meant "a kind, appearance", from specere "to look".
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「种类、外貌」，由 specere「看」派生。

items.en: Late Latin specificus meant "constituting a kind of its own", used in philosophical and medical texts.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 specificus 意为「自成一种的」，用于哲学与医学文本。

items.en: Medieval physicians used specific remedies aimed at one disease, giving the word its medical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪医师使用针对单一疾病的 specific 药物，赋予该词医学义项。

items.en: The word entered English in the seventeenth century with both the logical and the medical senses.
items.cn: 该词于十七世纪进入英语，兼具逻辑义与医学义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same seeing-and-naming family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for the exact and the particular.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「观看—指名」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示精确、特定的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning clearly or especially; built directly from specific.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「明确地；特别地」，由 specific 直接构成。

entries.definition: A written statement of exact details or requirements.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规格、说明书」，写明确切细节。

entries.definition: A sample taken for study; from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标本、样本」，出自同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The quality of being precise or unique to a target.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「明确性、特异性」。

entries.definition: A baby's dummy or something that calms; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「安抚奶嘴、安抚者」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Fully correct and precise in every detail; stronger than specific.
entries.definitionCN: 在每个细节上都完全正确精确，比 specific 更强。

entries.definition: Referring to one individual case out of many.
entries.definitionCN: 指众多之中某一单独的情形。

entries.definition: Carefully exact in measurement or statement.
entries.definitionCN: 在度量或表述上仔细而精确。

entries.definition: Clearly fixed and not likely to change.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚确定、不易改变的。

entries.definition: Stated openly and clearly, leaving nothing implied.
entries.definitionCN: 公开清楚地陈述，不留任何含蓄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and common phrases containing the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及包含该词的常见搭配。

normal.en: specere is to look: to be specific is to look closely enough to name one thing.
normal.cn: specere 意为「看」：做到 specific 就是看得足够近，从而指名一个事物。

normal.en: The same family gives specify, specifically and specification.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 specify、specifically、specification。

normal.en: Be specific about the details, not about vague hopes.
normal.cn: 对细节要明确，不要停留在模糊的期望上。

normal.en: A remedy once called specific aims at exactly one disease.
normal.cn: 昔日称为 specific 的药专治一种病。

normal.en: Specific to means belonging only to that one thing.
normal.cn: specific to 表示只属于那一个事物。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a printed page: one word swells while the rest blur.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜压在书页上：一个词变大，其余模糊。

abstract.en: Being specific is like aiming a flashlight: the beam covers one target only.
abstract.cn: 做到 specific 就像打手电：光束只罩住一个目标。

abstract.en: Vague answers scatter like sand; specific answers click into one slot.
abstract.cn: 模糊的回答像散沙，具体的回答咔哒落入唯一的槽。

examples.en: She asked for specific instructions on assembling the shelf.
examples.cn: 她要求给出组装书架的具体说明。

examples.en: The allergy is specific to peanuts and tree nuts.

senses.title: For one particular purpose
senses.definition: for one particular purpose or use and no other
senses.definitionCN: 专为某一特定目的或用途，不含其他
senses.example: The grant was given specifically for clean-water projects.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款是专门用于清洁饮水项目的。
senses.why: The finger lands on one name in a long list: the aim excludes everything else.
senses.whyCN: 手指落在长名单上的一个名字：这一指向排除其他一切。

senses.title: In a clear and exact way
senses.definition: in a manner that is clear, exact, and free of vagueness
senses.definitionCN: 以清楚、确切、不含糊的方式
senses.example: She specifically mentioned the broken window in her report.
senses.exampleCN: 她在报告中明确提到了那扇破窗。
senses.why: Precision is an adverb too: not only what is said, but how tightly it is said.
senses.whyCN: 精确也可以是副词：不仅在于说什么，还在于说得多紧。

senses.title: As an intensifier singling out
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something applies to one case especially
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某事尤其适用于某一情形
senses.example: The book was written specifically for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是专为初学者写的。
senses.why: The pointing finger presses harder: not just one case, but only that case.
senses.whyCN: 指点的手指更用力：不只是一个情形，而是只有那个情形。

senses.title: To narrow a statement further
senses.definition: used when making a previous statement more exact, often as more specifically
senses.definitionCN: 用于把先前的表述说得更确切，常用 more specifically
senses.example: The road passes farmland; more specifically, abandoned orchards.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路穿过农田；更确切地说，是废弃的果园。
senses.why: Each narrowing is one more click of the lens toward the single point.
senses.whyCN: 每收窄一次，镜头就向唯一点再拧近一格。

senses.title: In stated detail, item by item
senses.definition: with each item stated in detail rather than left general
senses.definitionCN: 逐项详述而非笼统带过
senses.example: The safety rules were specifically listed in the manual.
senses.exampleCN: 安全规则在手册中被逐项明确列出。
senses.why: The lens moves down the list, lighting one line after another.
senses.whyCN: 放大镜沿清单下移，逐行照亮。

senses.title: By name and not by description
senses.definition: by naming the very thing, instead of describing a class of things
senses.definitionCN: 指名确切对象，而非描述一类东西
senses.example: The rule named the bridge specifically, not bridges in general.
senses.exampleCN: 规则具体指名了那座桥，而不是泛指桥梁。
senses.why: Naming is the sharpest form of pointing: no description, just the name.
senses.whyCN: 指名是最锋利的指点方式：没有描述，只有名字。

senses.title: In technical usage: for a defined target
senses.titleCN: 技术用法：针对既定目标
senses.definition: in technical language, directed at a clearly defined target or condition
senses.definitionCN: 在技术语言中，指向清晰界定的目标或条件
senses.example: The antenna is tuned specifically to this frequency band.
senses.exampleCN: 这根天线专门调谐到这个频段。
senses.why: Engineering borrows the pointing image: the beam goes to one defined target.
senses.whyCN: 工程学借用指向意象：波束只射向一个既定目标。

senses.title: When excluding by contrast
senses.definition: used to contrast the named case with everything not named
senses.definitionCN: 用于把被指名的情形与其他未指名者对比
senses.example: The discount applies to students specifically, not to staff.
senses.exampleCN: 折扣只面向学生，不面向教职工。
senses.why: The single lit point defines a dark background: what is excluded sharpens what is chosen.
senses.whyCN: 唯一被照亮之点界定了黑暗背景：被排除者使被选择者更清晰。

senses.title: To state exactly and clearly
senses.definition: to say or write something in a precise, unmistakable form
senses.definitionCN: 以精确、不含糊的形式说出或写下
senses.example: The contract specifies the delivery date in bold letters.
senses.exampleCN: 合同以粗体字写明交货日期。
senses.why: The pen writes one line per requirement: nothing is left to guess.
senses.whyCN: 笔为每条要求各写一行：不留下任何猜测。

senses.title: To name the very thing required
senses.definition: to identify the exact thing wanted rather than a general class
senses.definitionCN: 指明确切所需之物，而非笼统一类
senses.example: The recipe specifies unsalted butter, not any butter.
senses.exampleCN: 食谱指定无盐黄油，而不是任何黄油。
senses.why: Naming beats describing: the pointed finger touches one object only.
senses.whyCN: 指名胜于描述：手指只触到一个对象。

senses.title: To set out requirements item by item
senses.definition: to list conditions, measurements, or parts one by one
senses.definitionCN: 把条件、尺寸或部件逐条列出
senses.example: The engineer specified each bolt size for the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师逐条列明框架的每个螺栓尺寸。
senses.why: The list grows line by line until the whole design is pinned down.
senses.whyCN: 清单逐行增长，直至整个设计被钉牢。

senses.title: To fix a time or amount
senses.definition: to settle an exact date, time, or quantity in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先确定确切的日期、时间或数量
senses.example: The invitation specified half past seven, not later.
senses.exampleCN: 请柬指定七点半，不得更晚。
senses.why: Numbers and dates are pinned like headings on the written page.
senses.whyCN: 数字与日期像标题一样钉在书面上。

senses.title: In law and contracts: to define terms
senses.definition: to define terms, obligations, or boundaries in a formal document
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文件中界定条款、义务或边界
senses.example: The lease specifies who repairs the heating system.
senses.exampleCN: 租约明确了暖气系统由谁维修。
senses.why: In documents, each line written is a line that cannot be argued later.
senses.whyCN: 在文件中，写下的每一行都是日后无从争辩的一行。

senses.title: In computing and data: to declare parameters
senses.definition: to declare exact parameters, values, or formats in a system or command
senses.definitionCN: 在系统或命令中声明确切的参数、数值或格式
senses.example: The script specifies the output folder and file name.
senses.exampleCN: 脚本指定了输出文件夹和文件名。
senses.why: Machines obey only what is written exactly; vagueness breaks the run.
senses.whyCN: 机器只服从写得确切的东西；含糊会让运行中断。

senses.title: To describe a method precisely
senses.definition: to lay out a procedure or method in exact steps
senses.definitionCN: 以确切步骤铺陈程序或方法
senses.example: The lab manual specifies the order of every reagent added.
senses.exampleCN: 实验手册规定了加入每种试剂的顺序。
senses.why: Steps written in order leave no room for improvisation.
senses.whyCN: 按序写明的步骤不给临场发挥留余地。

senses.title: To make plans definite for others
senses.definition: to fix a plan so that others can act on it without asking
senses.definitionCN: 把计划确定下来，使他人无需再问即可执行
senses.example: The architect specified the exact width of every doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师规定了每个门洞的确切宽度。
senses.why: A plan written precisely travels without its author: the lines speak for him.
senses.whyCN: 写得精确的计划无需作者同行：图纸上的线条替他说话。

normal.cn: 动词在 specific 上加 -fy「使」：使陈述变得具体明确。

normal.en: Unless otherwise specified is the classic contract phrase.
normal.cn: unless otherwise specified 是经典合同用语。

normal.en: Specify what, when, and how much: the verb loves details.
normal.cn: specify 说清是什么、何时、多少：这个动词热爱细节。

normal.en: The same family gives specific, specifically and specification.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 specific、specifically、specification。

normal.en: A specified amount is one written down exactly in advance.
normal.cn: specified amount 指事先确切写明的数额。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint with every blank already filled: nothing left for the builder to guess.
abstract.cn: 想象一张所有空白都已填好的图纸：施工者无从猜测。

abstract.en: To specify is to trade vagueness for a numbered list.
abstract.cn: specify 就是用一张编号清单换走含糊。

abstract.en: The pen that specifies draws a fence around misunderstanding.
abstract.cn: 用于 specify 的笔在误解周围画下围栏。

examples.en: The form asks you to specify your preferred contact method.
examples.cn: 表格要求你指定首选的联系方式。

examples.en: Safety rules specify that helmets must be worn at all times.
examples.cn: 安全规程明确规定必须始终佩戴头盔。

examples.en: Please specify which version of the software you are using.
examples.cn: 请注明你使用的是哪个版本的软件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比西法爱」——白纸黑字一条条写死：具体指定

root: 英语动词 specify 由 specific 加动词后缀 -fy 构成；specific 经晚期拉丁语 specificus 追溯至 species「种类」与 specere「观看」；一般认为印欧词根 *spek- 表示「观察」，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of specify all write the exact thing down: naming, listing, fixing times, defining terms, or declaring parameters.
sensesIntro.cn: specify 的各项义项都在把确切之物写下来：指名、列项、定时、界定条款或声明参数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand filling every blank line of a blueprint so nothing is left to guess.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把图纸上的每条空行都填满，不留下任何猜测。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT LINE: exact words replace vague gestures.
branches.cn: 陈述线：确切的词语取代含糊的手势。

branches.en: THE LIST LINE: item after item, and steps in fixed order.
branches.cn: 清单线：逐项铺陈，步骤按固定顺序。

branches.en: THE FIXING LINE: dates and amounts are pinned in advance.
branches.cn: 定时线：日期与数额事先钉死。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT LINE: written lines in contracts cannot be argued later.
branches.cn: 文件线：合同中写下的行文日后无从争辩。

branches.en: THE MACHINE-AND-PLAN LINE: parameters declared and plans fixed let others act without asking.
branches.cn: 机器与计划线：声明参数、定死计划，他人无需再问即可执行。

intro.en: Specify pairs the Latin kind-root with an English verb suffix; the family then branches regularly.
intro.cn: specify 把拉丁「种类」词根与英语动词后缀配对；词族随后规则分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin species, specere and Medieval Latin specificare are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species、specere 与中世纪拉丁语 specificare 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.example: The root anchors the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 该词根是整个词族的锚。

items.meaning: to state in terms of a specific kind
items.example: It is the direct model of specify.
items.exampleCN: 它是 specify 的直接来源。
它构成 specify 与 clarify。
它构成 specification 与 clarification。

items.example: The same seeing root gives spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 同一「观看」词根给出 spectacle。

latinEntries.meaning: to state in terms of a specific kind

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「规格；说明书；明确说明」
同族形容词，义为「明确的；特定的」
同族副词，义为「明确地；特意地」
由同族形容词加后缀构成，义为「明确性；特异性」

definition_zh: 言语；说话能力；演说；发言；方言
definition_en: the ability to speak, or a formal talk given to an audience
core_image: 台上一个人对着话筒开口：声音从喉咙走进人群
scene: 礼堂安静下来，所有人望向讲台。The mayor opened the ceremony with a short speech about the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 speech 是「演说、发言」（第 1 个义项：面向听众的正式讲话）；句意为市长以一段关于洪灾的简短致辞开启典礼。图中可辨识物件：讲台、话筒、礼堂。

pos.zh: 名词：言语；演说；说话能力；方言

derivatives.zh: 本词的同源动词基础，义为「说话；讲话」
由本词加后缀 -less 构成，义为「说不出话的；无言的」
由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「高谈阔论（含贬义）」
由 speak 加施动后缀构成，义为「说话者；扬声器」

senses.title: A formal talk to an audience
senses.definition: a formal talk delivered to an audience on a set occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在特定场合向听众发表的正式讲话
senses.example: Her graduation speech moved many parents to tears.
senses.exampleCN: 她的毕业致辞让许多家长落泪。
senses.why: The mouth faces a crowd: the voice is organized on purpose, not just let out.
senses.whyCN: 嘴巴面向人群：声音被有意组织起来，而不是随意发出。

senses.title: The ability to speak
senses.definition: the human ability to produce words with the voice
senses.definitionCN: 人类用声音产出词语的能力
senses.example: The stroke damaged the area of the brain that controls speech.
senses.exampleCN: 中风损伤了控制言语的大脑区域。
senses.why: Before any talk there is the power to talk; the instrument itself is named.
senses.whyCN: 在任何讲话之前先有讲话的能力；这里指名的是那件「乐器」本身。

senses.title: The way a person or group speaks
senses.definition: a person's or group's characteristic manner of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体特有的说话方式
senses.example: His speech still carries the accent of his hometown.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话仍带着家乡口音。
senses.why: Each voice prints its own pattern on the words it releases.
senses.whyCN: 每个声音在它释放的词语上印下自己的纹路。

senses.title: A dialect or language of a region
senses.definition: the language or dialect spoken in a particular place or community
senses.definitionCN: 特定地方或群体所说的语言或方言
senses.example: The novel records the speech of the fishing villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说记录了渔村的方言。
senses.why: A community's voice is a kind of speech, older than any textbook.
senses.whyCN: 社群的声音是一种言语，比任何教科书都古老。

senses.title: Words in grammar: part of speech
senses.definition: in grammar, one of the classes into which words are divided, as in part of speech
senses.definitionCN: 语法中词的分类之一，如 part of speech
senses.example: The teacher asked us to name the part of speech of each word.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要求我们说出每个词的词性。
senses.why: Even single words have a position in the order of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 即使单个词在言语秩序中也有位置。

senses.title: An utterance or passage of spoken words
senses.definition: an utterance or set of spoken words by one speaker, as in a play or record
senses.definitionCN: 单个说话者说出的一段话，如剧本或录音中
senses.example: The villain's final speech fills two whole pages.
senses.exampleCN: 反派最后的台词足足两页。
senses.why: A line of script belongs to one mouth until the curtain falls.
senses.whyCN: 剧本里的一席话属于一张嘴，直到落幕。

senses.title: Freedom of speech as a right
senses.definition: the legal right to express opinions publicly, as in freedom of speech
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达意见的法律权利，如言论自由
senses.example: The court defended freedom of speech in its ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在裁决中维护了言论自由。
senses.why: The power to speak becomes a right the law must guard.
senses.whyCN: 说话的能力变成法律必须守护的权利。

senses.title: Speechless: speech at its limit
senses.definition: in the word speechless, the state where speech has stopped
senses.definitionCN: 在 speechless 一词中，指言语停止的状态
senses.example: The news left her speechless for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 消息让她整整一分钟说不出话。
senses.why: The negative suffix shows the boundary: where speech ends, silence begins.
senses.whyCN: 否定后缀标出边界：言语止处，沉默开始。

intro.en: Speech is the native English noun of the speaking family, grown from an old verb of utterance.
intro.cn: speech 是「说话」词族的本土英语名词，从一个古老的「说出」动词生长而来。

items.en: *sprekan- is generally reconstructed as "to speak"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *sprekan- 表示「说话」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English had spæc "speech, utterance", related to the verb sprecan "to speak".
items.cn: 古英语有 spæc「言语、话语」，与动词 sprecan「说话」相关。

items.en: The form developed to speech through regular sound change in English.
items.cn: 该形式经英语规则的音变发展为 speech。

items.en: In Middle English, speech covered talk, dialect and formal address.
items.cn: 中古英语中，speech 覆盖谈话、方言与正式演说。

items.en: The word now names ability, oratory, grammar classes and legal rights.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它既指能力、演说，也指语法词类与法律权利。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the speaking family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for talk and address.
note.cn: 形近组收「说话」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示谈话与致辞的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning unable to speak; built from speech plus -less.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说不出话的」，由 speech 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to talk; the noun grew from it.
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词，义为「说话」，本名词由它派生。

entries.definition: An informal verb meaning to make long-winded speeches.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式动词，义为「高谈阔论」。

entries.definition: A burst of unrestrained activity; merely looks somewhat similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「狂欢、放纵的一阵」；只是外形略近，词源不同。

entries.definition: One who speaks, or the device that plays sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「说话者；扬声器」。

entries.definition: A formal talk, often ceremonial; overlaps the oratory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式讲话，常具仪式性，与演说义项重叠。

entries.definition: A general word for speaking or an informal lecture.
entries.definitionCN: 表示说话或非正式讲座的通用词。

entries.definition: A structured talk that teaches, often academic.
entries.definitionCN: 以讲授为主的结构化讲话，常属学术场合。

entries.definition: The art of public speaking; more abstract than speech.
entries.definitionCN: 公开演说的技艺，比 speech 更抽象。

entries.definition: Anything actually said, however small; overlaps the passage sense.
entries.definitionCN: 实际说出的话语，不论长短，与「一段话」义项重叠。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real speaking family and the phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的「说话」词族，以及该名词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Speech grew from the verb speak: one who speaks produces speech.
normal.cn: speech 由动词 speak 生长而来：说话者产出言语。

normal.en: Give a speech is the standard phrase for public address.
normal.cn: give a speech 是发表演说的标准搭配。

normal.en: Part of speech is the grammar class of a word.
normal.cn: part of speech 指词的语法类别。

normal.en: Speechless is speech plus -less: without speech.
normal.cn: speechless 由 speech 加 -less 构成：无言。

normal.en: Free speech names the legal right to speak freely.
normal.cn: free speech 指自由发言的法律权利。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone that turns breath into order: scattered thoughts become lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一只话筒把呼吸变成秩序：散乱的想法变成一行行字。

abstract.en: Speech is the bridge between one skull and another.
abstract.cn: 言语是连接两颗头颅之间的桥。

abstract.en: When speech fails, the body still speaks: hands, eyes, silence.
abstract.cn: 言语失灵时，身体仍在说话：手、眼睛、沉默。

examples.en: The candidate gave a speech about housing prices.
examples.cn: 候选人发表了一场关于房价的演说。

examples.en: A mild illness affected the child's speech for a while.
examples.cn: 一场小病在一段时间内影响了孩子的言语。

examples.en: His speech revealed that he came from the south coast.
examples.cn: 他的口音显示他来自南部海岸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比迟」——话筒一张口全场安静：演说；言语

root: speech 来自古英语 spæc「言语」，与动词 sprecan「说话」同源，属日耳曼语本土词；一般认为原始日耳曼语 *sprekan- 表示「说话」，更早来源不确定。拉丁语系同义的 loqui 一族与它无关。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of speech move outward from the voice: formal address, the ability behind it, personal and regional manners, grammar and rights.
sensesIntro.cn: speech 的义项从声音向外铺开：正式致辞、背后的能力、个人与地方口吻、语法与权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a microphone on a stand, and a crowd waiting for the first word.
core.cn: 核心意象：立架上的一只话筒，人群等待第一个字。

branches.en: THE STAGE LINE: organized words face a crowd, on stage or on the page.
branches.cn: 舞台线：组织好的语言面向人群，在台上或纸页上。

branches.en: THE POWER LINE: the ability to speak becomes a right the law defends.
branches.cn: 能力线：说话的能力变成法律守护的权利。

branches.en: THE MARK LINE: a voice prints its accent and dialect on every word.
branches.cn: 印记线：声音把口音与方言印在每个词上。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR LINE: even single words hold a seat in the order of speech.
branches.cn: 语法线：单个词也在言语秩序中占一席。

branches.en: THE LIMIT LINE: speechless marks where speech stops and silence takes over.
branches.cn: 边界线：speechless 标出言语止处、沉默接管。

intro.en: Speech is a bare native noun; English adds its own suffixes around it.
intro.cn: speech 本身是本土裸名词；英语用自家后缀在其周围构词。

latinIntro.en: Speech is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: speech 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的基础。

items.example: The noun keeps the vowel of the old past-participle line.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了旧分词一系的元音。

items.example: The Old English verb underlies the family.
items.exampleCN: 古英语动词是词族的基础。

items.example: The German cognate keeps the old root.
items.exampleCN: 德语同源词保留了古老词根。

derivatives.zh: 本词的同源动词基础，义为「说话；讲话」
由本词加后缀 -less 构成，义为「说不出话的；无言的」
由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「高谈阔论（含贬义）」

definition_zh: 速度；快速；变速；加速行进；成功率（摄影术语）
definition_en: the rate at which something moves or happens, or to move quickly
core_image: 里程表的指针爬升：时间被压成一条直线
scene: 雨夜的高速公路上，仪表盘发出微光。The sports car began to speed along the empty motorway.
sceneCN: 这里 speed 是「加速行进、超速行驶」（第 3 个义项：快速移动）；句意为跑车开始在空旷的高速公路上疾驰。图中可辨识物件：仪表盘、方向盘、雨刮。

pos.zh: 名词：速度；快速；快门速度
动词：加速行进；超速行驶；使加速

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「快速的；及时的」
由动词加名词化后缀构成，义为「超速行驶」
由本词加 meter 构成，义为「速度计；里程表」
由本词加 way 构成，义为「高速车道；赛车跑道」

senses.title: The rate of movement
senses.definition: the rate at which someone or something moves or travels
senses.definitionCN: 人或物移动、行进的快慢
senses.example: The train reached a speed of three hundred kilometres per hour.
senses.exampleCN: 列车时速达到三百公里。
senses.why: The needle on the dial answers one question only: how fast, right now.
senses.whyCN: 表盘上的指针只回答一个问题：此刻有多快。

senses.title: Rapidity of action or change
senses.definition: the quality of happening or being done quickly
senses.definitionCN: 发生或完成得快的性质
senses.example: Customers praised the speed of the delivery service.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客称赞该配送服务的快捷。
senses.why: A dial can measure deeds as well as wheels: work done fast reads as high speed.
senses.whyCN: 表盘既能量车轮也能量作为：做得快就是读数高。

senses.title: To move or travel quickly
senses.definition: to move, travel, or drive very quickly, sometimes breaking the limit
senses.definitionCN: 非常快速地移动、行进或驾驶，有时超限
senses.example: The ambulance sped through the quiet streets.
senses.exampleCN: 救护车疾驰穿过安静的街道。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: the needle climbs because the vehicle hurries.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：指针爬升，因为车辆在赶路。

senses.title: To make faster
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or move faster, as in speed up
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生或移动得更快，如 speed up
senses.example: The new software sped up the whole workflow.
senses.exampleCN: 新软件加快了整个工作流程。
senses.why: A hand can push the needle: whatever speeds up a thing hastens its motion.
senses.whyCN: 有一只手能推动指针：凡使某物 speed up，就催促了它的运动。

senses.title: Breaking a speed limit
senses.definition: to drive faster than the legal limit allows
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶速度快于法定限速
senses.example: He was fined for speeding near the school zone.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校附近因超速被罚款。
senses.why: Beyond the marked line on the dial, the law starts counting.
senses.whyCN: 越过表盘上的标线，法律开始计数。

senses.title: A gear setting on a machine
senses.definition: one of the gear settings on a bicycle or machine, as in a ten-speed bicycle
senses.definitionCN: 自行车或机器上的挡位设置之一，如十速自行车
senses.example: She shifted into a lower speed for the uphill road.
senses.exampleCN: 上坡路时她换入了低速挡。
senses.why: Each setting is one notch on the dial's ladder.
senses.whyCN: 每个挡位就是表盘阶梯上的一格。

senses.title: Shutter speed in photography
senses.definition: in photography, the length of time a camera shutter stays open
senses.definitionCN: 摄影中相机快门开启的时长
senses.example: A fast shutter speed froze the hummingbird's wings.
senses.exampleCN: 高速快门凝固了蜂鸟的翅膀。
senses.why: Light through the lens is timed like traffic through a gate.
senses.whyCN: 透过镜头的光像过闸的车流一样被计时。

senses.title: Success or prosperity in old phrases
senses.definition: in old-fashioned phrases like God speed, success or good fortune
senses.definitionCN: 在 God speed 等旧式用语中表示成功或好运
senses.example: The letter closed with the old wish, God speed.
senses.exampleCN: 信的结尾写着旧式的祝愿：God speed。
senses.why: Before engines, speed meant the wish that your journey go well and succeed.
senses.whyCN: 在发动机之前，speed 意为祝愿旅程顺利、获得成功。

intro.en: Speed is a native English word whose oldest meaning was not fastness but success.
intro.cn: speed 是本土英语词，其最古老的意义不是「快」，而是「成功」。

items.en: *spōdiz is generally reconstructed as "success, luck"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spōdiz 表示「成功、运气」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spēd meant "success, prosperity, quick progress".
items.cn: 古英语 spēd 意为「成功、兴旺、迅速的进展」。

items.en: The verb spēdian meant "to succeed, to prosper, to hasten".
items.cn: 动词 spēdian 意为「成功、兴旺、加快」。

items.en: In Middle English the sense of quick movement came to dominate the older sense of success.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，「快速移动」义逐渐压过古老的「成功」义。

items.en: The word now serves engines, cameras, law and everyday talk alike.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词服务于发动机、相机、法律与日常口语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the native Germanic family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for rate and haste.

entries.definition: An adjective meaning quick or done without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「快速的、及时的」。

entries.definition: The device that measures speed; a compound of speed and meter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「速度计」，由 speed 与 meter 复合。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of speed.
entries.definitionCN: speed 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: A plant's seed; merely one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「种子」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: The Middle English spelling of speed, kept in old texts.
entries.definitionCN: speed 的中古英语拼法，见于旧文本。

entries.definition: Speed with a direction, used in physics; more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 带方向的速率，用于物理学，更专业。

entries.definition: The speed of walking, working, or change; often steady.
entries.definitionCN: 行走、工作或变化的快慢，常指稳定节奏。

entries.definition: Great hurry, sometimes careless; overlaps the rapidity sense.
entries.definitionCN: 匆忙急促，有时失之草率，与「迅速」义项重叠。

entries.definition: Urgent quickness, often as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 急急忙忙，常用作动词。

entries.definition: Literary quickness of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 文学化的快速。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real native family and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的本土词族，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Speed up is the verb phrase for going faster.
normal.cn: speed up 是「加速」的动词短语。

normal.en: The old past form is sped: the ambulance sped by.
normal.cn: 旧过去式是 sped：救护车疾驰而过。

normal.en: Speed limit marks the legal ceiling on the dial.
normal.cn: speed limit 是表盘上的法定上限。

normal.en: God speed keeps the ancient sense of success.
normal.cn: God speed 保留「成功」的古义。

normal.en: Speedometer is speed plus meter, the measuring device.
normal.cn: speedometer 由 speed 加 meter 构成，即测量仪器。

abstract.en: Picture a needle climbing a dial: every turn of the wheel shows on the gauge.
abstract.cn: 想象指针沿表盘爬升：车轮每转一圈都显示在刻度上。

abstract.en: Speed compresses distance: what was far arrives near.
abstract.cn: 速度压缩距离：远的抵达变近。

abstract.en: The old wish God speed travels like a thrown coin into a departing road.
abstract.cn: 旧祝愿 God speed 像一枚掷向远行之路的硬币。

examples.en: The wind increased the speed of the spreading fire.
examples.cn: 大风加快了火势蔓延的速度。

examples.en: She sped past the slow trucks on the ring road.
examples.cn: 她在环路上疾速超过了慢速卡车。

examples.en: Choose a shutter speed suitable for low light.
examples.cn: 选择适合弱光环境的快门速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比得」——指针爬表盘一路向前：速度；疾驰

root: speed 属日耳曼语本土词：古英语 spēd「成功、兴旺」来自动词 spēdian「成功、加快」，一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spōdiz 意为「成功、运气」，更早来源不确定；「快速」义是中古英语时期发展出的新重心。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of speed spin out from one dial: rate of travel, rapidity of deeds, the verb of hurrying, gears, cameras and an old wish of success.
sensesIntro.cn: speed 的各项义项沿一块表盘展开：行进的速率、作为的迅速、赶路的动词、挡位、相机，以及一句古老的祝愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle climbing a dial while wheels hum below.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针沿表盘爬升，车轮在下方嗡鸣。

branches.en: THE RATE LINE: how fast a wheel turns or a deed gets done.
branches.cn: 速率线：车轮转多快，事做得多快。

branches.en: THE VERB LINE: the thing itself hurries, or a hand pushes it faster.
branches.cn: 动词线：事物自己赶路，或被手催促加快。

branches.en: THE LAW-AND-GEAR LINE: limits count past the marked line, and gears notch the ladder.
branches.cn: 法律与挡位线：越过标线即计数，挡位标出阶梯。

branches.en: THE LENS LINE: light is timed through the camera gate.
branches.cn: 镜头线：光在相机闸口被计时。

branches.en: THE OLD WISH LINE: before engines, speed meant success on the road.
branches.cn: 古愿线：在发动机之前，speed 意为一路成功。

intro.en: Speed is a bare native root; compounds and suffixes gather around it.
intro.cn: speed 是本土裸词根；复合词与后缀围绕它聚集。

latinIntro.en: Speed is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: speed 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

scene: 教室的黑板分成两栏，一边字母一边口诀。The teacher asked the boy to spell the word island on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 spell 是「拼写」（第 1 个义项：逐个说出或写出字母）；句意为老师让男孩在黑板上拼写 island 一词。图中可辨识物件：黑板、板擦、粉笔。

senses.title: To write or name letters in order
senses.definition: to say or write the letters of a word in the correct order
senses.definitionCN: 按正确顺序说出或写出单词的字母
senses.example: Can you spell your surname for the receptionist?
senses.exampleCN: 你能为前台拼写你的姓氏吗？
senses.why: The pen drops one letter into each cell until the word stands complete.
senses.whyCN: 笔把一个字母逐格放入，直到词语完整立起。

senses.title: To have letters arranged in a certain way
senses.definition: to have or form words with particular letters, as in a word spelled wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 以特定字母组成词语，如拼写错误
senses.example: The place name is spelled two different ways on old maps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地名在旧地图上有两种拼法。
senses.why: The same letter-chain can rest in more than one grid.
senses.whyCN: 同一串字母可以落进不止一种格子。

senses.title: A period of time of a kind
senses.definition: a short, unbroken period of a particular activity, weather, or state
senses.definitionCN: 某活动、天气或状态的短暂连续时段
senses.example: After a long spell of rain, the fields turned green.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间的降雨过后，田野变绿了。
senses.why: A different old word rests here: a shift of work, a stretch of hours.
senses.whyCN: 这里停着另一个旧词：一轮换班、一段时辰。

senses.title: Magic words with power
senses.definition: a set of words believed to have magical power
senses.definitionCN: 被认为具有魔力的一组词语
senses.example: The witch murmured a spell over the boiling pot.
senses.exampleCN: 女巫对着沸腾的锅念咒语。
senses.why: Old belief says a word said just right bends the world; the letters themselves were once thought to carry force.
senses.whyCN: 古老的信仰认为，话说得恰到好处就能扭转世界；字母本身曾被认为带有力量。

senses.title: A magical influence or charm
senses.definition: a strong attraction or influence as if caused by magic
senses.definitionCN: 如魔法般的强烈吸引力或影响
senses.example: The violinist held the audience under a spell.
senses.exampleCN: 小提琴手让观众如中魔咒般着迷。
senses.why: The magic words widen: anything that grips a crowd works like a charm.
senses.whyCN: 魔法之词扩展：凡能摄住人群者皆如咒语。

senses.title: To take turns doing something
senses.definition: to take turns with another person at a task
senses.definitionCN: 与他人轮流承担一项任务
senses.example: The rowers spelled each other at the oars.
senses.exampleCN: 划手们轮流换桨。
senses.why: A shift of workers is a shift of the word: one rests while one holds.
senses.whyCN: 换班是词义的换班：一人休息，一人持守。

senses.title: To result in something bad
senses.definition: to have something, usually something unpleasant, as a result
senses.definitionCN: 导致某种结果，通常是不好的结果
senses.example: Ignored warnings spell disaster for any project.
senses.exampleCN: 被忽视的警告对任何项目都预示着灾难。
senses.why: Letters build a word; acts build a future, and the metaphor reads one as the other.
senses.whyCN: 字母拼成词，行为拼出未来，隐喻把二者互读。

senses.title: To read slowly letter by letter
senses.definition: to read or understand a text letter by letter, often in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 逐字母阅读或理解文本，多见于旧用法
senses.example: The child spelled out the sign one letter at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子一个字母一个字母地读出告示。
senses.why: Before fluent reading, every word must be climbed letter by letter.
senses.whyCN: 在流利阅读之前，每个词都要逐字母攀爬。

intro.en: Spell is two words that landed on one spelling: a Germanic verb of talking and a Roman letter-word.
intro.cn: spell 是两个词恰好落在同一拼法上：一个是日耳曼「讲述」动词，一个是罗马「字母」词。

items.en: *spellam is generally reconstructed as "saying, story"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spellam 表示「言说、故事」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spell meant "story, news, saying"; a spell was a tale told aloud.
items.cn: 古英语 spell 意为「故事、消息、话语」；spell 是被大声讲出的故事。

items.en: The letter sense came from Old French espeller, from Frankish, influenced by Latin littera-based usage; the sources link it to the same Germanic root for "saying".
items.cn: 「字母」义来自古法语 espeller，源于法兰克语，并受拉丁字母用语影响；各家将其与同一日耳曼「言说」词根相联系。

items.en: The compound gōdspell "good news" gave English gospel, keeping the old "story" sense.
items.cn: 复合词 gōdspell「好消息」给出英语 gospel，保留了古老的「故事」义。

items.en: Because spoken formulas were "sayings", spell came to mean magic words, and later charm.
items.cn: 由于口头咒语也是一种「言说」，spell 引申为咒语，再引申为魔力。

items.en: The period sense is usually traced to a different, related word for a shift or task, with later blending.
items.cn: 「一段时间」义通常追溯至另一个表示换班或任务的相关词，后期相互混合。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the saying family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for magic, periods, and lettering.
note.cn: 形近组收「言说」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收魔法、时段与拼字相关词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or way of writing letters.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指拼写行为或拼法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning fascinated as if by magic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「如被魔咒般着迷」。

entries.definition: Good news; a compound built with the old "story" word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「福音」，用古老的「故事」词复合而成。

entries.definition: A hard outer cover; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「贝壳、外壳」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A speaker who grips an audience like magic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指如施魔般摄住听众的演说者。

entries.definition: Chanting of magic words; overlaps the charm sense.
entries.definitionCN: 念诵咒文，与「咒语」义项重叠。

entries.definition: A magic formula or an attractive power.
entries.definitionCN: 咒符或迷人的力量。

entries.definition: A stretch of time; general word overlapping the interval sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，通用词，与「时段」义项重叠。

entries.definition: A fixed period of doing a job or duty.
entries.definitionCN: 承担某项工作或职责的固定时段。

entries.definition: To fill with delight as if by magic.
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷，如被施魔法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real histories behind the single spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用同一拼法背后的两条真实历史。

normal.en: The verb spell out literally names letters one by one.
normal.cn: 动词 spell out 字面上就是逐个报出字母。

normal.en: Gospel keeps the old sense of spell as story or news.
normal.cn: gospel 保留了 spell「故事、消息」的古义。

normal.en: Cast a spell on treats words as magic.
normal.cn: cast a spell on 把词语当作魔法。

normal.en: A spell of cold weather is one stretch of time.
normal.cn: a spell of cold weather 指一段寒冷天气。

normal.en: Spell trouble reads acts like letters that build a word.
normal.cn: spell trouble 把行为当作拼出结果的字母。

abstract.en: Picture two hands: one sets letters in a grid, the other stirs a pot while chanting.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手：一只把字母排进格子，一只一边念咒一边搅锅。

abstract.en: A word spelled right and a charm said right both believe order has power.
abstract.cn: 拼写正确的词与念诵得法的咒都相信：秩序即力量。

abstract.en: Time also spells itself out: one hour follows another like letters into cells.
abstract.cn: 时间也在自我拼写：一小时接一小时，如字母逐格落入。

examples.en: The child could spell her own name before school age.
examples.cn: 这孩子上学前就会拼写自己的名字。

examples.en: The heat wave brought a long spell of dry weather.
examples.cn: 热浪带来了一段漫长的干旱天气。

examples.en: Budget cuts spell trouble for the small theatre.
examples.cn: 预算削减给这家小剧院带来麻烦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯佩尔」——字母排格子，咒语念成诗：拼写；咒语

root: 英语 spell 实为两个来源的汇流：一为古英语 spell「故事、言说」（日耳曼词根，一般认为 *spellam 表示「言说」，更早来源不确定），发展出「咒语、魔力」义；一为经古法语 espeller 的「拼写」动词，二者拼写重合。「一段时间」义一般认为另源于表示换班任务的相关词，后期混合。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spell gather around one grid: letters into cells, words into magic, hours into stretches, and acts into consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: spell 的各项义项围绕同一张格子展开：字母入格、词语成咒、时辰成段、行为成后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grid of empty cells that letters, hours, and magic words can all fall into.
core.cn: 核心意象：一格格空格，字母、时辰与咒语都可逐格落入。

branches.en: THE LETTERING LINE: letters climb into cells, named, ordered, or read slowly.
branches.cn: 拼字线：字母逐格攀入，或报出、或按序、或慢读。

branches.en: THE CHARM LINE: the old "saying" turns into magic words and their grip on a crowd.
branches.cn: 咒语线：古老的「言说」变成咒语及其对人群的摄力。

branches.en: THE INTERVAL LINE: a stretch of hours falls into the grid like one long letter.
branches.cn: 时段线：一段时辰如一个长字母落入格子。

branches.en: THE SHIFT LINE: rowers take turns like letters taking their slots.
branches.cn: 换班线：划手轮换，如字母各就其位。

branches.en: THE RESULT LINE: acts spell futures as letters spell words.
branches.cn: 结果线：行为拼出未来，如字母拼出词语。

intro.en: Spell carries two histories at once, so its word family splits into a saying line and a lettering line.
intro.cn: spell 同时承载两条历史，其词族因此分为「言说」系与「拼字」系。

latinIntro.en: Spell is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: spell 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: The old noun underlies the magical senses.
items.exampleCN: 古名词是魔法诸义的基础。
这个复合词给出英语 gospel。

items.example: It fed the spelling sense of spell.
items.exampleCN: 它滋养了 spell 的拼写义。

definition_zh: 花费；花钱；度过；用尽；耗费（时间、精力）
definition_en: to pay out money, or to use or pass time and effort
core_image: 摊开的掌心：钱币与光阴都从这里漏出去
scene: 月底的账单摊在桌上，他在灯下一笔笔核对。The family spends most of its income on rent and food.
sceneCN: 这里 spend 是「花费、支出」（第 1 个义项：付出金钱）；句意为这家人的大部分收入花在房租和食物上。图中可辨识物件：账单、台灯、算盘。

senses.title: To pay out money
senses.definition: to give money to pay for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为购买商品或服务而付出金钱
senses.example: They spend nearly half their salary on childcare.
senses.exampleCN: 他们将近一半的工资花在托育上。
senses.why: The open palm lets coins fall: what is held is handed onward.
senses.whyCN: 摊开的掌心让钱币落下：持有之物被继续传递出去。

senses.title: To pass time
senses.definition: to use time doing something or remaining somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 以某方式用掉时间或停留某处
senses.example: We spent the whole afternoon in the old library.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在老图书馆度过了整个下午。
senses.why: Time is treated as currency: hours are coins the hand lets go.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作货币：小时就是掌中放开的硬币。

senses.title: To use up effort or energy
senses.definition: to use up strength, energy, or effort on something
senses.definitionCN: 把力气、精力或努力用在某事上
senses.example: The climbers spent all their strength before the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在登顶前耗尽了全部力气。
senses.why: The palm empties of everything it held: strength leaks like coins.
senses.whyCN: 掌心所握全部漏空：力气像钱币一样流走。

senses.title: To consume a resource
senses.definition: to use up supplies such as fuel, materials, or goodwill
senses.definitionCN: 用尽燃料、材料或善意等储备
senses.example: The long siege spent the city's food stores.
senses.exampleCN: 长期围困耗尽了城里的存粮。
senses.why: Whatever the hand holds can be spent: grain, fuel, patience.
senses.whyCN: 掌中所握皆可耗费：粮食、燃料、耐心。

senses.title: To pass a period of life somewhere
senses.definition: to live through a period of one's life in a place or state
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地方或状态中经历人生的一段时光
senses.example: She spent her childhood by the seaside.
senses.exampleCN: 她在海边度过了童年。
senses.why: Whole seasons become coins in the same open hand.
senses.whyCN: 整个季节也成了同一只摊开手掌中的硬币。

senses.title: To wear out by use
senses.definition: to wear something out by using it, often in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 因使用而使某物耗损，多见于旧用法
senses.example: The old mill had spent its gears after decades of grinding.
senses.exampleCN: 几十年的研磨使老磨坊的齿轮磨平了。
senses.why: Use is payment: each turn of the gear spends a little of itself.
senses.whyCN: 使用即支付：齿轮每转一圈就耗去自身一点。

senses.title: To expend formally or in accounts
senses.definition: to pay out or allocate money, especially in formal or written accounts
senses.definitionCN: 支出或划拨资金，尤指正式账目中
senses.example: The ministry spends its budget across twelve provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门把预算分配到十二个省。
senses.why: The palm becomes a ledger: each coin falls into a named column.
senses.whyCN: 掌心变成账本：每枚硬币落入一个有名字的栏。

senses.title: Spent: emptied of force
senses.definition: in the adjective spent, drained and no longer usable or effective
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 spent 表示枯竭、不再可用或有效
senses.example: The spent rocket fell silently into the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 燃尽的火箭无声坠入大海。
senses.why: The past participle names the palm after everything has fallen from it.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词指称一切落尽之后的掌心。

intro.en: Spend is a native English word whose Latin cousins gave English expense and expenditure.
intro.cn: spend 是本土英语词，其拉丁同族词给英语带来 expense 与 expenditure。

items.en: *spendan is generally reconstructed as "to pay out"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spendan 表示「付出」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spendan meant "to spend, expend", possibly influenced by Latin expendere "to weigh out, pay".
items.cn: 古英语 spendan 意为「花费、支出」，一般认为受过拉丁语 expendere「称量付出」的影响。

items.en: Latin expendere meant "to weigh out, pay out", from ex- "out" plus pendere "to hang, weigh".
items.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 意为「称量付出」，由 ex-「出」加 pendere「悬挂、称量」构成。

items.en: The pendere family also gave English pound, pension and spend's cousins expense and expend.
items.cn: pendere 词族还给出英语 pound、pension，以及 spend 的同族词 expense、expend。

items.en: The verb spread to time and strength: hours and effort are spent like coins.
items.cn: 动词扩展到时间与力气：小时与努力都像硬币一样被花掉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the paying-out family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of paying and passing.
note.cn: 形近组收「付出」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示支付与度过的动词。

entries.definition: The past form and an adjective meaning drained of force.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式形式，也作形容词，义为「力尽的」。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to pay out or use up; same Latin line.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，义为「支出、消耗」，同一拉丁词系。

entries.definition: The formal noun for money paid out.
entries.definitionCN: 正式名词，指支出的钱款。

entries.definition: To turn round and round; merely one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「旋转」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning costing much; from the same pendere family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昂贵的」，出自同一 pendere 词族。

entries.definition: The general verb for giving money owed or due.
entries.definitionCN: 支付应付款项的通用动词。

entries.definition: To require a payment; the price side of spending.
entries.definitionCN: 需要付出；花钱的「价格」一面。

entries.definition: To consume entirely; overlaps the exhaustion sense.
entries.definitionCN: 耗尽，与「用尽」义项重叠。

entries.definition: To go through time; overlaps the time sense.
entries.definitionCN: 度过时光，与「度过」义项重叠。

entries.definition: To use up resources, food, or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 消耗资源、食物或精力。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的 pendere 词族，以及该动词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spend money on is the money pattern; spend time doing is the time pattern.
normal.cn: spend money on 是钱的句型；spend time doing 是时间的句型。

normal.en: The past form is spent, and spent as adjective means drained.
normal.cn: 过去式是 spent，形容词 spent 意为力尽。

normal.en: The Latin cousin expendere also gives expense and expenditure.
normal.cn: 拉丁同源词 expendere 还给出 expense 与 expenditure。

normal.en: Spendthrift is the spender of thrift: one who wastes savings.
normal.cn: spendthrift 是挥霍 thrift 之人：浪费积蓄者。

normal.en: Spend the night treats hours as coins.
normal.cn: spend the night 把小时当作硬币。

abstract.en: Picture an open palm above a drain: coins, hours, and strength all slip through.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的掌心悬在排水口上：硬币、时辰与力气都从中滑落。

abstract.en: A ledger and a calendar are both spent from the same hand.
abstract.cn: 账本与日历都从同一只手中被花掉。

abstract.en: The spent rocket shows the palm after the last coin has fallen.
abstract.cn: 燃尽的火箭展示最后一枚硬币落尽后的掌心。

examples.en: The city spends millions on road repairs each year.
examples.cn: 这座城市每年在道路维修上花费数百万。

examples.en: He spent his youth working in shipyards.
examples.cn: 他在船厂劳作中度过了青年时代。

examples.en: After the race, the runners lay spent on the grass.
examples.cn: 比赛结束后，选手们力尽地躺在草地上。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spend all drain one palm: money, hours, strength, supplies, whole seasons, and finally the spent thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: spend 的各项义项都在排空同一只掌心：钱、时辰、力气、物资、整段岁月，最终是被耗尽之物本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open palm above a drain, letting coins and hours slip out together.
core.cn: 核心意象：排水口上摊开的掌心，硬币与时辰一同滑落。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: coins fall into shops or into named ledger columns.
branches.cn: 金钱线：硬币落入商店，或落入账本的有名栏。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: hours and whole seasons are spent like currency.
branches.cn: 时间线：小时与整段岁月像货币一样被花掉。

branches.en: THE STRENGTH LINE: effort and supplies leak away until nothing is held.
branches.cn: 力量线：力气与物资渐渐漏空，直至一无所有。

branches.en: THE WEAR LINE: each use pays a little of the tool itself.
branches.cn: 磨损线：每次使用都支付工具自身的一小部分。

branches.en: THE SPENT LINE: the past participle shows the palm after all has fallen.
branches.cn: 力尽线：过去分词展示一切落尽后的掌心。

intro.en: Spend is a native root with a Latin cousin; suffixes and compounds grow on both lines.
intro.cn: spend 是本土词根并有一个拉丁表亲；两条线上都长出后缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin expendere and its family are recorded; the Germanic root itself is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 及其词族均有记录；日耳曼词根本身为重构形式。

definition_en: to flow over the edge of a container accidentally, or to let a secret out
core_image: 杯口一斜，液体越过边缘流得到处都是
scene: 餐桌一角的水杯被袖子带歪了。Soup spilled onto the cloth as the waiter rushed over.
sceneCN: 这里 spill 是「洒出、溢出」（第 1 个义项：液体意外流出容器）；句意为汤洒到了桌布上。图中可辨识物件：餐桌、汤碗、桌布。

pos.zh: 及物动词：使洒出；使溢出

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词化后缀构成，义为「溢出效应；外溢影响」

senses.title: To flow over the edge accidentally
senses.definition: to flow or fall out of a container over its edge by accident
senses.definitionCN: 液体或物品因意外越过容器边缘流出或落下
senses.example: Milk spilled across the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶洒满了厨房地板。
senses.why: The tilted cup opens an unplanned path: what was held escapes its edge.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜的杯子开出一条计划外的路径：所持之物越过边缘逃走。

senses.title: To make a liquid overflow
senses.definition: to cause a liquid or contents to overflow from a container
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或内容物从容器中溢出
senses.example: He spilled coffee all over the keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 他把咖啡洒了满键盘。
senses.why: A hand, not chance, tips the cup this time.
senses.whyCN: 这次是手，不是运气，把杯子弄翻。

senses.title: To pour out in a flood
senses.definition: to pour out, flow out, or spread in large numbers or amounts
senses.definitionCN: 大量地流出、涌出或散开
senses.example: Crowds spilled out of the stadium gates.
senses.exampleCN: 人群从体育场大门涌出。
senses.why: The edge cannot hold what surges: people and light pour like liquid.
senses.whyCN: 边缘盛不下涌动之物：人群和光像液体一样倾泻。

senses.title: To reveal a secret
senses.definition: to let information escape from where it was kept, as in spill the beans
senses.definitionCN: 让消息从保存之处泄露，如 spill the beans
senses.example: One of the clerks finally spilled the secret to the press.
senses.exampleCN: 一名职员最终向媒体说漏了秘密。
senses.why: Information is treated like liquid in a jar: one tip and it runs.
senses.whyCN: 信息被当作罐中液体：一倾斜就流走。

senses.title: To scatter from a moving container
senses.definition: to scatter or fall out of a moving vehicle or holder
senses.definitionCN: 从行进的车辆或承载物中散落
senses.example: The truck spilled gravel across the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在转弯处撒了一路碎石。
senses.why: A moving edge shakes loose whatever it no longer grips.
senses.whyCN: 行进的边缘抖落一切它握不住的东西。

senses.title: A fall or tumble
senses.definition: a sudden fall from a bicycle, horse, or height
senses.definitionCN: 从自行车、马背或高处突然跌落
senses.example: The rider took a nasty spill on the gravel path.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手在碎石路上重重摔了一跤。
senses.why: What escapes the edge may be the rider: bodies spill as liquids do.
senses.whyCN: 越过边缘的可能是骑手：身体如液体般洒落。

senses.title: The amount that overflows
senses.definition: the amount of liquid or material that has overflowed
senses.definitionCN: 溢出的液体或材料量
senses.example: The crew cleaned an oil spill near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 船员清理了海岸附近的一次漏油。
senses.why: The escaped liquid becomes a thing itself, measured and mourned.
senses.whyCN: 逃逸的液体自成一物，被计量、被哀悼。

senses.title: To spill over into neighbouring areas
senses.definition: to extend beyond one place or situation and affect others, as in spill over
senses.definitionCN: 越过一处范围影响他处，如 spill over
senses.example: The border conflict spilled over into neighbouring districts.
senses.exampleCN: 边境冲突波及了邻近地区。
senses.why: Trouble ignores boundaries: it flows wherever the land tilts.
senses.whyCN: 麻烦无视边界：土地向哪里倾斜，它就流向哪里。

intro.en: Spill is a native English word whose old meaning was to destroy, before liquids took over the word.
intro.cn: spill 是本土英语词，其古老意义是「毁灭」，后来才被「液体」占用了这个词。

items.en: *spilthan- is generally reconstructed for "to destroy, kill"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spilthan- 表示「毁灭、杀」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spillan meant "to destroy, ruin, kill"; blood was spilled in battle in the old sense.
items.cn: 古英语 spillan 意为「毁灭、毁坏、杀」；旧义中「流血洒地」即出自此。

items.en: In Middle English the sense narrowed to letting liquids or grain escape a container.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，词义收窄为让液体或谷物从容器流失。

items.en: English kept both spilled and spilt, the -t form stronger in British usage.
items.cn: 英语同时保留 spilled 与 spilt 两种形式，-t 形式在英式用法中更强。

items.en: The word now covers liquids, crowds, secrets, oil and even stock-market spillover.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词涵盖液体、人群、秘密、石油乃至股市外溢。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the native family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of overflowing and leaking.
note.cn: 形近组收本土词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示溢出与泄漏的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for effects that spread beyond their first place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指超出原地的外溢影响。

entries.definition: British past form of spill, also used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: spill 的英式过去形式，也作形容词。

entries.definition: A channel that lets excess water escape a dam.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指让水库多余水泄出的溢洪道。

entries.definition: Quiet or continuing; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「静止的、仍然」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sharp point or sudden rise; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「尖刺、骤增」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: To flow beyond the brim; overlaps the liquid sense.
entries.definitionCN: 越过边缘流出，与液体义项重叠。

entries.definition: To escape through a hole, of liquids or secrets.
entries.definitionCN: 液体或秘密经孔洞逸出。

entries.definition: To flow in a stream, deliberately or heavily.
entries.definitionCN: 成流涌出，或有意或倾盆。

entries.definition: To let fall or lose naturally, as leaves or tears.
entries.definitionCN: 自然落下或失去，如落叶、落泪。

entries.definition: To spread widely in different directions.
entries.definitionCN: 向不同方向散开。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real old sense and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古义，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spill the beans is the famous idiom for telling secrets.
normal.cn: spill the beans 是「说漏嘴」的著名习语。

normal.en: The old sense was destroy: spill blood once meant kill.
normal.cn: 古义是毁灭：spill blood 曾指杀戮。

normal.en: Spill over means trouble flows past its border.
normal.cn: spill over 表示麻烦流过边界。

normal.en: Oil spill names one of the worst accidents at sea.
normal.cn: oil spill 指海上最严重的事故之一。

normal.en: British English often uses spilt as the past form.
normal.cn: 英式英语常用 spilt 作过去式。

abstract.en: Picture every edge in the world as a brim waiting for one tilt.
abstract.cn: 想象世上每条边缘都是一道杯沿，等待一次倾斜。

abstract.en: Secrets behave like ink: once spilled, no cloth restores the page.
abstract.cn: 秘密像墨水：一旦洒出，任何布都无法复原纸页。

abstract.en: A crowd held too long behind gates spills the moment they open.
abstract.cn: 在闸门后憋得太久的人群，开门一刻便涌出。

examples.en: She spilled juice on the report this morning.
examples.cn: 她今早把果汁洒在了报告上。

examples.en: Light spilled from every window of the tall building.
examples.cn: 高楼每扇窗都透出灯光。

examples.en: The oil spill damaged hundreds of kilometres of coastline.
examples.cn: 漏油事故破坏了数百公里海岸线。

root: spill 属日耳曼语本土词：古英语 spillan「毁灭、毁坏」，一般认为源于原始日耳曼语 *spilthan-「毁灭」，更早来源不确定；中古英语起词义收窄为「溢出、洒出」，古老的「流血毁灭」义仍留痕于 spill blood。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spill all cross an edge: liquids over brims, crowds past gates, secrets out of jars, and trouble past borders.
sensesIntro.cn: spill 的各项义项都在跨越一条边缘：液体越过杯沿、人群涌过闸门、秘密溜出罐口、麻烦漫过边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tilted cup whose brim can no longer hold what it carries.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只倾斜的杯子，边缘再也盛不住所载之物。

branches.en: THE LIQUID LINE: what escapes is measured, cleaned, or mourned.
branches.cn: 液体线：逃逸之物被计量、清理或哀悼。

branches.en: THE FLOOD LINE: crowds, light and gravel pour like liquid over edges.
branches.cn: 倾泻线：人群、光与碎石如液体般越过边缘。

branches.en: THE SECRET LINE: information tips out of its jar with one careless move.
branches.cn: 泄密线：信息一次不慎便从罐中倾出。

branches.en: THE FALL LINE: bodies spill too, from saddles and bicycles.
branches.cn: 跌落线：身体也会洒落，从马背与自行车上。

branches.en: THE BORDER LINE: trouble spills over into the next valley and the next market.
branches.cn: 边界线：麻烦漫入下一座山谷与下一个市场。

senses.title: To turn round and round
senses.definition: to turn quickly around a central point or axis
senses.definitionCN: 围绕中心点或轴快速转动
senses.example: The fans spun above the hot courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 风扇在闷热的法庭上方旋转。
senses.why: One point holds still while the rest sweeps circles around it.
senses.whyCN: 一点静止，其余围绕它画圆。

senses.title: To twist fibres into thread
senses.definition: to draw out and twist fibres such as wool into thread
senses.definitionCN: 把羊毛等纤维拉出并捻成线
senses.example: Her grandmother could spin wool into fine thread.
senses.exampleCN: 她祖母能把羊毛纺成细线。
senses.why: The same circling motion twists loose fibres into one held line.
senses.whyCN: 同样的旋转动作把松散纤维捻成一条被握住的线。

senses.title: To seem to whirl before the eyes
senses.definition: to seem to whirl, as when a person feels dizzy
senses.definitionCN: 似在旋转，如人感到头晕时
senses.example: The room began to spin after the fairground ride.
senses.exampleCN: 玩过游乐设施后，房间开始天旋地转。
senses.why: The world itself seems to take up the spinning.
senses.whyCN: 世界仿佛自己也转了起来。

senses.title: To move swiftly in a vehicle
senses.definition: to ride or drive swiftly, often for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 乘车疾驰，常为消遣
senses.example: They took the old car out for a spin along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开着旧车沿海岸兜风。
senses.why: Wheels spinning carry the rider out of the ordinary road.
senses.whyCN: 旋转的车轮把乘坐者带出日常之路。

senses.title: To present facts favourably
senses.definition: to present information in a way that favours one side
senses.definitionCN: 以偏向一方的方式呈现信息
senses.example: The office spun the poor figures as steady progress.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室把糟糕的数据粉饰成稳步推进。
senses.why: The twisting motion turns plain facts into a shaped line, like fibre into thread.
senses.whyCN: 扭转的动作把平实事实捻成有形状的线，如纤维成线。

senses.title: To invent or tell a story
senses.definition: to tell or invent a story, as in spin a yarn
senses.definitionCN: 讲述或编造故事，如 spin a yarn
senses.example: The old sailor spun a yarn about a sea serpent.
senses.exampleCN: 老水手编了个海蛇的故事。
senses.why: Storytelling and threading share the same word: a tale is spun from loose talk.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事与纺线共用一词：故事由散漫话语捻成。

senses.title: A rapid turning movement
senses.definition: a quick turning movement around a central axis
senses.definitionCN: 围绕中轴的快速转动
senses.example: The skater finished with a graceful spin.
senses.exampleCN: 滑冰者以一个优雅的旋转收尾。
senses.why: The verb freezes into a noun: the circle itself is named.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝为名词：圆周本身被指名。

senses.title: A derivative product or company
senses.definition: a new product or company developed from an existing one, as in spin-off
senses.definitionCN: 由既有产品或公司派生的新产品或新公司，如 spin-off
senses.example: The research lab produced several useful spin-offs.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究实验室产出了几个有用的副产品。
senses.why: The thread spun from the main yarn becomes its own cloth.
senses.whyCN: 从主线捻出的线自成一块布。

intro.en: Spin is a native English word of the thread and wheel world, rooted in the old craft of twisting fibre.
intro.cn: spin 是本土英语词，属于线与轮的世界，根植于捻纤维的古老手艺。

items.en: *spinnan- is generally reconstructed as "to draw out and twist thread"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spinnan- 表示「拉出并捻线」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spinnan meant "to spin thread", the everyday work of households.
items.cn: 古英语 spinnan 意为「纺线」，是家家户户的日常劳作。

items.en: The agent noun spinne gave English spinster, once simply a woman who spun.
items.cn: 施动名词 spinne 给出英语 spinster，本义仅为纺纱女子。

items.en: The sense widened to whirling motion, dizziness, and swift riding.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，词义扩展到旋转、眩晕与疾驰。

items.en: Politics added the sense of favourable presentation, and business the spin-off.
items.cn: 政治领域加上了粉饰义，商业领域则产生了 spin-off。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the native twisting family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for turning and twisting.
note.cn: 形近组收本土「捻线」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示转动与扭转的词。

entries.definition: One who spins thread, or a device that spins.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指纺纱工或旋转装置。

entries.definition: Once a woman who spun wool; now an unmarried woman in older usage.
entries.definitionCN: 原指纺纱女子，旧用法中指未婚女子。

entries.definition: A product or company derived from an existing one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指由既有事物派生的产品或公司。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of spin.
entries.definitionCN: spin 的过去式与分词。

entries.definition: The backbone of a body or book; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「脊柱、书脊」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To turn around an axis, often regular and measured.
entries.definitionCN: 绕轴转动，常有规律、可测量。

entries.definition: To orbit or turn around a centre.
entries.definitionCN: 环绕中心运行或转动。

entries.definition: To wind threads or parts together; overlaps the fibre sense.
entries.definitionCN: 把线或部件缠在一起，与纤维义项重叠。

entries.definition: To turn rapidly and confusedly; overlaps the dizzy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 急速而纷乱地转，与眩晕义项重叠。

entries.definition: To move or turn as if on wheels.
entries.definitionCN: 如车轮般移动或转动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real spinning craft and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的纺纱手艺，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spin a yarn is the idiom that keeps the old thread craft.
normal.cn: spin a yarn 是保留古老纺线手艺的习语。

normal.en: The past form is spun: the wheel spun all night.
normal.cn: 过去式是 spun：车轮转了一整夜。

normal.en: Spinster began as simply a woman who spun.
normal.cn: spinster 起初仅指纺纱的女子。

normal.en: Go for a spin means a short fast drive.
normal.cn: go for a spin 指一次短途疾驰。

normal.en: A spin-off is thread twisted off the main yarn.
normal.cn: spin-off 是从主线捻出的线。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip on a coin: one held point, everything else circling.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按住一枚硬币：一点被按住，其余画圆。

abstract.en: A story is wool in the hand: loose until spun into a line.
abstract.cn: 故事如掌中羊毛：捻成线之前是散的。

abstract.en: When the room spins, the axis has slipped out of your ear.
abstract.cn: 房间旋转时，轴线从你的耳中滑脱了。

examples.en: The wheels of the cart spun wildly in the mud.
examples.cn: 车轮在泥中疯狂空转。

examples.en: She spun the wool into a strong warm thread.
examples.cn: 她把羊毛纺成结实保暖的线。

examples.en: The agency spun the data to protect its budget.
examples.cn: 该机构粉饰数据以保住预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯宾」——指尖捻动转出圆，羊毛捻成线：旋转；纺纱

root: spin 属日耳曼语本土词：古英语 spinnan「纺线」，一般认为源于原始日耳曼语 *spinnan-「拉出并捻线」，更早来源不确定；旋转、眩晕与疾驰诸义均为纺纱这一旋转动作的延伸。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spin all turn one axis: wheels, threads, dizzy rooms, fast cars, shaped stories and new companies.
sensesIntro.cn: spin 的各项义项都绕同一根轴转：车轮、线、眩晕的房间、疾驰的车、成形的故事与新公司。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a held centre with everything else sweeping circles around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一点被握住，其余围绕它画圆。

branches.en: THE MOTION LINE: wheels, dizzy rooms and skater turns share one circling centre.
branches.cn: 运动线：车轮、眩晕的房间与滑冰转体共享同一圆心。

branches.en: THE THREAD LINE: fibre, tales and facts are twisted into one held line.
branches.cn: 纺线线：纤维、故事与事实被捻成一条被握住的线。

branches.en: THE ROAD LINE: spinning wheels carry riders swiftly out of the ordinary.
branches.cn: 道路线：旋转的车轮载着乘坐者疾速脱离日常。

branches.en: THE PRESENTATION LINE: facts are shaped like fibre to favour one side.
branches.cn: 陈述线：事实像纤维一样被捻向有利一方。

branches.en: THE OFFSHOOT LINE: thread spun off the main yarn becomes its own cloth.
branches.cn: 派生线：从主线捻出的线自成一块布。

intro.en: Spin is a bare native root; compounds and agent nouns gather around it.
intro.cn: spin 是本土裸词根；复合词与施动名词围绕它聚集。

latinIntro.en: Spin is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: spin 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

The vowel change marks the old strong verb.
items.exampleCN: 元音变化标出古老强变化动词。

items.example: The idiom joins the two main senses.
items.exampleCN: 该习语连接两个主要义项。

The Old English verb is the direct source.

definition_en: the non-physical part of a person, or the mood and energy of a person or group
core_image: 身体里那口看不见的气：它抬着头，扛着一整个人
