senses.title: Energy, courage, and mood
senses.definition: the energy, courage, and cheerfulness that make a person or group act
senses.definitionCN: 使人或群体行动起来的能量、勇气与愉快心情
senses.example: The team showed real spirit in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队在下半场表现出真正的斗志。
senses.why: The invisible breath inside lifts the body: it is the head that refuses to fall.
senses.whyCN: 体内的无形之气托起身体：是不肯低头的那个「头」。

senses.title: The soul as opposed to the body
senses.titleCN: 灵魂；与肉体相对的心灵
senses.definition: the part of a person that is not the body and is thought to live on
senses.definitionCN: 人的非肉体部分，被认为可延续
senses.example: Many faiths hold that the spirit outlives the body.
senses.exampleCN: 许多信仰认为灵魂比肉体长久。
senses.why: What leaves last from a dying body was imagined as breath going out.
senses.whyCN: 垂死之身最后离开之物，被想象为呼出的一口气。

senses.title: A ghost or supernatural being
senses.definition: the soul of a dead person or a supernatural being
senses.definitionCN: 死者的魂灵或超自然存在
senses.example: Villagers said a spirit walked the old orchard at night.
senses.exampleCN: 村民说夜里有个幽灵走过老果园。
senses.why: The escaped breath keeps walking after the body stops.
senses.whyCN: 身体停了，那口逸出的气还在走。

senses.title: Mood of a group or time
senses.definition: the prevailing mood or attitude of a group, era, or place
senses.definitionCN: 群体、时代或地方的主导情绪或态度
senses.example: The reforms caught the spirit of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这些改革抓住了那个十年的时代精神。
senses.why: One breath can be shared: a whole crowd inhales the same mood.
senses.whyCN: 一口气可以被共享：整个人群吸入同一种情绪。

senses.title: The real meaning behind words
senses.definition: the real intention or meaning behind a rule or statement, as in the spirit of the law
senses.definitionCN: 规则或陈述背后的真实意图，如 the spirit of the law
senses.example: He obeyed the letter but broke the spirit of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他遵守了字面，却违背了协议的实质。
senses.why: The life inside the words matters more than their shell.
senses.whyCN: 词语内部的生命比外壳更重要。

senses.title: Strong alcoholic drink
senses.definition: a strong distilled alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin
senses.definitionCN: 威士忌、金酒等烈性蒸馏酒
senses.example: The cupboard held several bottles of spirits.
senses.exampleCN: 柜子里有几瓶烈酒。
senses.why: The word for the life-breath was pressed into the bottle: liquor lifts or sinks the inner breath.
senses.whyCN: 指生命之气的词被压进瓶子：酒能提起或压沉体内那口气。

senses.title: To carry off mysteriously
senses.definition: to take someone away quickly and secretly, as in spirit away
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而秘密地把人带走，如 spirit away
senses.example: The children were spirited away to a safe farmhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被悄悄转移到安全的农舍。
senses.why: A person vanishes like a soul leaving the body: taken by unseen hands.
senses.whyCN: 人如灵魂离体般消失：被看不见的手带走。

senses.title: Vital force in living things
senses.definition: the animating force of living things, as in the spirits of the forest
senses.definitionCN: 赋予生物生气的力量，如森林之灵
senses.example: Old tales gave every river a guardian spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 古老传说给每条河都配了一位守护神灵。
senses.why: Breath was the sign of life, so life itself got the word.
senses.whyCN: 气息是生命的标记，于是生命本身也得了这个词。

intro.en: Spirit is the Latin word for breath, and every modern sense still moves like an exhale.
intro.cn: spirit 是拉丁语的「气息」一词，其每个现代义项仍像一次呼气。

items.en: (s)peis- is generally reconstructed as "to blow, breathe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 (s)peis- 表示「吹、呼吸」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin spiritus meant "breath, breathing", later "life, courage, soul".
items.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus 意为「气息、呼吸」，后指「生命、勇气、灵魂」。

items.en: The verb spirare meant "to breathe", and it also gives inspire, respire and expire.
items.cn: 动词 spirare 意为「呼吸」，还给出 inspire、respire 与 expire。

items.en: Old French esprit carried the word toward English with soul and vigour senses joined.
items.cn: 古法语 esprit 把灵魂与活力两义一并带入英语路径。

items.en: English took spirit in the thirteenth century, first in religious texts.
items.cn: 英语于十三世纪吸收 spirit，最早见于宗教文本。

items.en: Distilled liquor was later called spirits, and modern speech added team spirit and spin.
items.cn: 蒸馏酒后来被称为 spirits；现代用语又添 team spirit 等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the breathing family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for soul and mood.
note.cn: 形近组收「呼吸」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示灵魂与情绪的词。

entries.definition: An adjective of the soul and the inner life.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指灵魂与内在生活。

entries.definition: Full of energy and courage, as in a spirited debate.
entries.definitionCN: 精力与勇气充沛，如 spirited debate。

entries.definition: To put spirit into someone; to encourage.
entries.definitionCN: 把精神注入某人；鼓舞。

entries.definition: To breathe into someone a feeling or idea.
entries.definitionCN: 把情感或想法如气息般吹入人心。

entries.definition: A winding curve; merely looks somewhat similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「螺旋」；只是外形略近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The inner self, often with moral weight.
entries.definitionCN: 内在自我，常带道德分量。

entries.definition: The mind and inner self in psychological language.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学语言中的心灵与内在自我。

entries.definition: The confidence of a group, as of troops or staff.
entries.definitionCN: 群体的信心，如部队或员工。

entries.definition: The core nature of something; overlaps the real-meaning sense.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的核心本质，与「真义」义项重叠。

entries.definition: The visible soul of the dead; narrower than spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 死者显形的魂灵，比 spirit 范围窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real breath root and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的「呼吸」词根，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spirit is Latin spiritus: the breath that animates a body.
normal.cn: spirit 即拉丁语 spiritus：赋予身体生气的气息。

normal.en: The same root gives inspire, respire and expire.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 inspire、respire、expire。

normal.en: In high spirits means cheerful and full of energy.
normal.cn: in high spirits 指情绪高涨、精力充沛。

normal.en: Spirits on a bar menu mean strong distilled drinks.
normal.cn: 酒吧单上的 spirits 指烈性蒸馏酒。

normal.en: Spirit away means to remove someone secretly.
normal.cn: spirit away 指秘密带走某人。

abstract.en: Picture a flame above a candle: not the wax, but the thing that dances on it.
abstract.cn: 想象蜡烛上方的火焰：不是蜡，而是在蜡上起舞之物。

abstract.en: A rule has a letter and a breath; obedience without breath obeys nothing.
abstract.cn: 规则有字母也有气息；没有气息的服从什么也没服从。

abstract.en: Distilled grain holds one glassful of life-breath; drink it and the breath lifts, then sinks.
abstract.cn: 蒸馏谷物盛着一杯生命之气；饮下则气息先扬后沉。

examples.en: The volunteers worked with great spirit through the night.
examples.cn: 志愿者们整夜斗志昂扬地工作。

examples.en: The play caught the restless spirit of the 1960s.
examples.cn: 这部剧捕捉了六十年代躁动的时代精神。

examples.en: They obeyed the rules but missed their spirit entirely.
examples.cn: 他们遵守了规则，却完全错失其精神实质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯皮瑞特」——一息尚存昂着头：精神；灵魂

root: 拉丁语 spiritus「气息、呼吸」由动词 spirare「呼吸」派生，一般认为源于原始印欧语 (s)peis-「吹、呼吸」，更早来源不确定；经古法语 esprit 于十三世纪进入英语，由「气息」生长出「灵魂、精神、烈酒」诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spirit all breathe: the inner force of a person, the shared mood of a crowd, the meaning inside rules, and even the lift inside a bottle.
sensesIntro.cn: spirit 的各项义项都在呼吸：人的内在力量、群体的共同情绪、规则的内里真义，乃至瓶中被提起的那口气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flame of breath standing upright inside a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：体内一小簇直立呼吸的火焰。

branches.en: THE LIVING FORCE LINE: the breath animates one body or a whole imagined forest.
branches.cn: 生命力线：气息赋予一个身体乃至想象中的整个森林生气。

branches.en: THE SOUL LINE: what escapes the body may live on, or walk at night.
branches.cn: 灵魂线：离开身体之气可以延续，或在夜里行走。

branches.en: THE SHARED LINE: crowds inhale one mood; rules hold a breath inside their letters.
branches.cn: 共享线：人群吸入同一情绪；规则的字母内藏一口气。

branches.en: THE BOTTLE LINE: distilled grain keeps a glass of life-breath.
branches.cn: 瓶中线：蒸馏谷物盛着一杯生命之气。

branches.en: THE VANISHING LINE: to spirit away is to remove a person like a soul leaving a body.
branches.cn: 消隐线：spirit away 是如灵魂离体般把人带走。

intro.en: Spirit is a Latin noun with a living verb family around it in English.
intro.cn: spirit 是拉丁名词，英语中围绕它有一个活的动词家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin spiritus and spirare are well recorded; only the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus 与 spirare 均有充分记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的词根。

items.example: The noun passed into English as spirit.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词以 spirit 进入英语。
它构成 inspire 与 inspirit。

items.example: It forms conspire, to breathe together.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 conspire「共谋」，即一同呼吸。

items.example: It forms respire, to breathe again.
It forms expire, to breathe out.

由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「精神的；心灵的」

definition_zh: 精神的；心灵的；宗教的；与灵魂有关的；（名）黑人灵歌
definition_en: connected with the human spirit or soul rather than the body or material things
core_image: 身体之外的那部分人：摸不着，却撑着人站直
scene: 山间小教堂的木窗透进晨光。The choir sang a spiritual about crossing the river home.
sceneCN: 这里 spiritual 是「灵歌」（第 5 个义项：宗教歌曲，多指黑人灵歌）；句意为唱诗班演唱了一首关于渡河归家的灵歌。图中可辨识物件：小教堂、木窗、唱诗班。

pos.zh: 形容词：精神的；心灵的；宗教的
名词：灵歌（多指黑人灵歌）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「在精神上」
本词的名词基础，义为「精神；灵魂」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「灵性；精神性」
由同族名词加后缀构成，义为「精神饱满的」

senses.title: Of the spirit rather than the body
senses.definition: relating to the spirit or soul rather than to the body or physical things
senses.definitionCN: 与精神或灵魂相关，而非身体或物质
senses.example: Music met her spiritual needs after the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 病后音乐满足了她的精神需求。
senses.why: The hand cannot grasp this part of a person: it stands where matter ends.
senses.whyCN: 手抓不住人的这一部分：它站在物质尽头之处。

senses.title: Of religion or sacred things
senses.definition: connected with religion or the sacred
senses.definitionCN: 与宗教或神圣之事相关
senses.example: The temple is the spiritual centre of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这座寺庙是山谷的宗教中心。
senses.why: The breath within becomes breath before the divine.
senses.whyCN: 体内之气化为面对神圣的呼吸。

senses.title: Of inner growth and depth
senses.definition: concerned with inner development, meaning, or depth of life
senses.definitionCN: 关乎内在发展、生命意义或深度
senses.example: His journals record a slow spiritual awakening.
senses.exampleCN: 他的日记记录了一场缓慢的心灵觉醒。
senses.why: The hidden person grows like roots below the visible stem.
senses.whyCN: 隐藏之人如可见茎干下的根系在生长。

senses.title: Not material or worldly
senses.definition: not made of matter or tied to worldly concerns
senses.definitionCN: 不由物质构成，不系于世俗关切
senses.example: The letter speaks of wealth that is spiritual, not gold.
senses.exampleCN: 信中所言财富是精神的，而非黄金。
senses.why: What has no weight may still be the heaviest thing a person owns.
senses.whyCN: 没有重量的东西可能是一个人所拥有的最重之物。

senses.title: A religious song, especially a Black spiritual
senses.definition: a religious folk song, especially one created by enslaved African Americans
senses.definitionCN: 宗教民歌，尤指被奴役的非裔美国人创作的歌曲
senses.example: The choir performed old spirituals at the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班在音乐节上演唱了古老的灵歌。
senses.why: The adjective freezes into a noun: the sacred breath takes the form of song.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝为名词：神圣的呼吸化为歌的形式。

senses.title: Clerical or church-related
senses.definition: belonging to the church or its ministry rather than civil affairs
senses.definitionCN: 属于教会及其神职而非世俗事务
senses.example: The court gave the church spiritual jurisdiction over marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 法院给予教会对婚姻的宗教管辖权。
senses.why: The inner realm gets its own government, beside the state.
senses.whyCN: 内在领域在国家之外另立治理。

senses.title: Living, quickening, as breath
senses.definition: giving life or liveliness, in older or literary usage
senses.definitionCN: 赋予生命或生气，见于旧用法或文学用法
senses.example: The poet calls sleep the spiritual restoration of the weary.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人称睡眠为疲惫者灵性的复原。
senses.why: Breath was the sign of life, so whatever quickens a thing is spiritual.
senses.whyCN: 气息是生命的标记，故凡赋予生气者皆为 spiritual。

senses.title: Immaterial beings and their realm
senses.definition: belonging to immaterial beings or their world
senses.definitionCN: 属于非物质存在或其世界
senses.example: Old stories fill the hills with spiritual presences.
senses.exampleCN: 古老故事里满是山间的灵性存在。
senses.why: The breath that outlives the body gathers into an unseen realm.
senses.whyCN: 比身体长存之气聚成一个看不见的领域。

intro.en: Spiritual is the adjective of the Latin breath-word, carried into English through church Latin.
intro.cn: spiritual 是拉丁「气息」词的形容词形式，经教会拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: (s)peis- is generally reconstructed as "to blow, breathe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 (s)peis- 表示「吹、呼吸」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin spiritus meant "breath", later "soul, courage".
items.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus 意为「气息」，后指「灵魂、勇气」。

items.en: Late Latin spiritualis meant "of the spirit, of the breath", used heavily by church writers.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 spiritualis 意为「属于灵的、属于气息的」，教会作家大量使用。

items.en: The word moved through Old French spirituel and ecclesiastical Latin into English.
items.cn: 该词经古法语 spirituel 与教会拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: English spiritual first marked the religious sphere, later inner life and the song tradition.
items.cn: 英语 spiritual 最早标示宗教领域，后指内在生活与灵歌传统。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the breathing family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words of the inner and sacred life.
note.cn: 形近组收「呼吸」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示内在与神圣生活的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being concerned with the spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指关注精神的性质。

entries.definition: Full of energy; shares the same noun base spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛；与 spiritual 共享名词基础 spirit。

entries.definition: To encourage; built on the same breath-word.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓舞；建立在同一「气息」词上。

entries.definition: An adjective of strong liquor; same family, different branch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指烈酒的；同族而分支不同。

entries.definition: A ceremonial act; merely looks somewhat similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「仪式」；只是外形略近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Of organized faith; overlaps the sacred sense.
entries.definitionCN: 属于制度性信仰，与「神圣」义项重叠。

entries.definition: Set apart for holy use or respect.
entries.definitionCN: 为神圣用途或敬重而区分开。

entries.definition: Inside the self, especially in feeling or life.
entries.definitionCN: 自我内部，尤指情感或生活层面。

entries.definition: Light, airy, and immaterial; overlaps the immaterial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 轻盈缥缈、非物质，与「非物质」义项重叠。

entries.definition: Going beyond ordinary experience or matter.
entries.definitionCN: 超越日常经验或物质。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real breath root and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的「呼吸」词根，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spiritual is spirit plus -ual: of the breath, of the soul.
normal.cn: spiritual 由 spirit 加 -ual 构成：属于气息、属于灵魂。

normal.en: Spiritual needs are needs no shop can sell.
normal.cn: spiritual needs 是商店无法出售的需求。

normal.en: A spiritual in music is a sacred folk song.
normal.cn: 音乐中的 spiritual 是神圣的民歌。

normal.en: The same family gives spirituality and spirituous.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 spirituality 与 spirituous。

normal.en: Spiritual jurisdiction once meant the church court's realm.
normal.cn: spiritual jurisdiction 曾指教会法庭的领域。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing in two worlds: feet on soil, head in moving air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人立于两界：脚在土上，头在流动的气中。

abstract.en: The part of you that cannot be photographed is the spiritual part.
abstract.cn: 无法被拍摄的那部分你，就是 spiritual 部分。

abstract.en: A song that carries the breath of a suffering people is called a spiritual.
abstract.cn: 承载受难民族气息的歌，被称为灵歌。

examples.en: Reading was for him a form of spiritual exercise.
examples.cn: 对他而言，阅读是一种心灵锻炼。

examples.en: The spirituals preserved stories of hope and escape.
examples.cn: 这些灵歌保存了希望与出逃的故事。

examples.en: The town built a hospital for physical and spiritual care.
examples.cn: 小镇建起一座兼顾身体与心灵照护的医院。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯皮瑞丘尔」——身体之外撑起人：精神的；灵歌

root: spiritual 由 spirit 加形容词后缀 -ual 构成；spirit 来自拉丁语 spiritus「气息」，由 spirare「呼吸」派生，一般认为源于原始印欧语 (s)peis-「吹、呼吸」，更早来源不确定；晚期拉丁语 spiritualis 为教会用语，经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spiritual climb from the breath upward: the inner person, the sacred, the immaterial, and the song that carries it all.
sensesIntro.cn: spiritual 的各项义项从气息向上攀：内在之人、神圣、非物质，以及承载这一切的歌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with feet on soil and head breathing in moving air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人脚踩泥土，头在流动的气中呼吸。

branches.en: THE INNER LINE: needs and growth that no market can weigh.
branches.cn: 内在线：市场无法称量的需求与成长。

branches.en: THE SACRED LINE: the divine realm and the church jurisdiction that guards it.
branches.cn: 神圣线：神圣领域及守护它的教会管辖权。

branches.en: THE IMMATERIAL LINE: weightless wealth and unseen presences in the hills.
branches.cn: 非物质线：无重量的财富与山间无形的存在。

branches.en: THE QUICKENING LINE: whatever gives life is breath, and breath is spirit.
branches.cn: 赋生线：凡赋予生命者皆气息，气息即灵。

branches.en: THE SONG LINE: the adjective freezes into the noun for sacred folk song.
branches.cn: 歌线：形容词凝为名词，指神圣的民歌。

intro.en: Spiritual stacks the Latin breath-word with an adjective suffix, and English keeps branching it.
intro.cn: spiritual 把拉丁「气息」词与形容词后缀叠合；英语继续在其上分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin spiritus, spirare and Late Latin spiritualis are recorded; the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus、spirare 与晚期拉丁语 spiritualis 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: It formed spiritualis in Late Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它在晚期拉丁语中构成 spiritualis。

items.example: It forms spirituous of strong drink.

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 spiritus 的来源。

items.example: It shares the noun base spirit.
items.exampleCN: 它与 spiritual 共享名词基础。

items.example: It puts spirit into a person.

definition_zh: 恶意；怨恨；不顾；刁难
definition_en: a desire to hurt, annoy, or offend someone, or in spite of: without being affected by
core_image: 一只故意推倒积木塔的手：不为得到什么，只为看它倒下
scene: 游乐场角落，积木塔立得高高的。The boy knocked over the tower out of pure spite.
sceneCN: 这里 spite 是「恶意」（第 1 个义项：故意伤人的心思）；句意为男孩纯粹出于恶意推倒了积木塔。图中可辨识物件：积木塔、游乐场、沙坑。

pos.zh: 短语介词 in spite of：不顾；尽管

collocations.phrase: cut off one's nose to spite one's face

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「怀恶意的；恶毒的」
由 spiteful 加副词后缀构成，义为「恶毒地」
由 spiteful 加名词后缀构成，义为「恶毒；怨恨」
同源词，义为「尽管；不顾」

senses.title: A desire to hurt or annoy
senses.definition: a desire to hurt, annoy, or offend another person, often without gain to oneself
senses.definitionCN: 想伤害、惹恼或冒犯他人之心，常于己无利
senses.example: He broke the window out of sheer spite.
senses.exampleCN: 他纯粹出于恶意打破了窗户。
senses.why: The hand pushes the tower not to build anything but to watch it fall.
senses.whyCN: 这只手推倒塔不是为建造什么，而是为看它倒塌。

senses.title: Ill will from a grudge
senses.definition: bitter ill will built up from past grievances
senses.definitionCN: 由旧怨积累的恶感
senses.example: She signed the letter out of old spite from their quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 她因争吵留下的旧怨带着恶意写了这封信。
senses.why: A wound that keeps hurting feeds its own small anger.
senses.whyCN: 持续作痛的伤口喂养着它自己的小小怒火。

senses.title: In spite of: despite
senses.definition: used before a fact that does not prevent the main statement, meaning despite
senses.definitionCN: 用于不阻止主句成立的事实之前，意为「尽管」
senses.example: In spite of the rain, the match went on.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，比赛照常进行。
senses.why: The obstacle stands in the sentence, yet the deed walks straight past it.
senses.whyCN: 句中立着障碍，行为却径直走过它。

senses.title: To annoy or thwart someone
senses.definition: to deliberately annoy or frustrate someone
senses.definitionCN: 蓄意惹恼或挫败某人
senses.example: The children spited each other with small tricks all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们整个下午用小恶作剧互相刁难。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: the push itself is given a name.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：推搡这个动作本身得了名字。

senses.title: Petty revenge in sayings
senses.definition: self-harming revenge, as in cut off your nose to spite your face
senses.definitionCN: 伤己式的报复，如「割鼻损面」之说
senses.example: Refusing the cheap ticket just to punish the airline was cutting off his nose to spite his face.
senses.exampleCN: 为惩罚航空公司而拒绝廉价机票，只是损人不成反害己。
senses.why: Old sayings warn that spite aimed at others often circles back home.
senses.whyCN: 古谚提醒：射向他人的恶意常绕回自己身上。

senses.title: Spite house or spite fence
senses.definition: a fence or building made purely to annoy neighbours
senses.definitionCN: 专为惹恼邻居而设的栅栏或建筑
senses.example: The tall spite fence went up the week after the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵过后一周，那道赌气的高栅栏立了起来。
senses.why: Even walls and lumber can carry a grudge.
senses.whyCN: 连墙与木料都能承载一段怨恨。

senses.title: In spite of oneself
senses.titleCN: in spite of oneself：不由自主
senses.definition: although one did not intend or want to
senses.definitionCN: 虽非本意、非其所愿
senses.example: She laughed in spite of herself at the silly joke.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个傻笑话，她不由自主地笑了。
senses.why: The obstacle here is one's own intention, and the laughter slips past it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍是自己的本意，笑声却溜了过去。

senses.title: Archaic: contempt or scorn
senses.definition: contempt or scorn in older literary usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧文学用法中的轻蔑
senses.example: Old poems spoke of doing a thing in spite of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 旧诗中常说「不顾世人白眼而行某事」。
senses.why: The oldest face of the word is a raised chin against the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的面孔是朝人群昂起的下巴。

intro.en: Spite began as a Latin word for contempt and shortened on its way into English.
intro.cn: spite 原是拉丁语中表示「轻蔑」的词，进入英语的路上被截短了。

items.en: *spei- is generally reconstructed as "to point, sharp"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spei- 表示「指向、尖」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin despicere meant "to look down on", from de- "down" plus specere "to look".
items.cn: 拉丁语 despicere 意为「俯视、轻看」，由 de-「向下」加 specere「看」构成。

items.en: Old French despit meant "contempt, scorn", the noun of despiter "to look down on".
items.cn: 古法语 despit 意为「轻蔑」，来自动词 despiter「轻看」。

items.en: English took despite, and spite was cut from it in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先收下 despite，十三世纪从中截出 spite。

items.en: The word now lives in malice and in the fixed phrase in spite of.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词既指恶意，也活在固定短语 in spite of 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of similar shape and the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers words for malice and defiance.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词与同一拉丁词族；近义组收表示恶意与违抗的词。

entries.definition: The fuller relative meaning despite; spite was cut from it.
entries.definitionCN: 更长的同族词，义为「尽管」，spite 即从它截出。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone full of spite.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容满心恶意的人。

entries.definition: To eject saliva; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「吐唾沫」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: A place or location; merely sounds alike and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「地点、场所」；仅读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small fairy or a soft-drink brand; letters rearranged and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「小精灵」或某汽水品牌；字母换序，词源不同。

entries.definition: A stronger, colder wish to harm; spite is often pettier and hotter.
entries.definitionCN: 更强烈冷酷的伤害之心；spite 常更琐碎、更外露。

entries.definition: A lasting resentment held over time, often quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 长久怀有的怨恨，常不外露。

entries.definition: Bitter indignation at unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 因不公对待而生的愤懑。

entries.definition: Open resistance; related to the despite line of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 公然违抗；与该词 despite 一脉相关。

entries.definition: The desire to get even for a wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 想为冤屈讨回公道的报复之心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real phrase in spite of and the image of the deliberate push.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实短语 in spite of，以及「故意一推」的意象。

normal.en: despite is the tall brother: spite was clipped off the front of it.
normal.cn: despite 是高个子兄弟：spite 就是从它前面截下来的。

normal.en: Out of spite means the only reason was the wish to annoy.
normal.cn: out of spite 意为唯一的动机就是想惹恼人。

normal.en: In spite of the storm, the ship sailed: the storm could not stop it.
normal.cn: in spite of the storm，船照样起航：风暴拦不住它。

normal.en: The same Latin root specere "to look" gives despise: to look down on.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词根 specere「看」给出 despise「轻视」，即往下看。

normal.en: Cutting off your nose to spite your face warns against self-harming anger.
normal.cn: 「割鼻损面」警醒人们勿以害己的方式泄愤。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching not for a prize but for a tower to topple.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸出去不为取物，只为推倒一座塔。

abstract.en: In spite of is a wall in the sentence that the sentence walks around.
abstract.cn: in spite of 是句中的一面墙，而句子绕过了它。

abstract.en: A grudge kept warm long enough turns into spite: cold anger that pushes.
abstract.cn: 怨恨保温够久就变成 spite：会出手推人的冷怒。

examples.en: He hid her tools out of spite, not necessity.
examples.cn: 他藏起她的工具是出于恶意，并非必要。

examples.en: In spite of the traffic, they arrived before the ceremony began.
examples.cn: 尽管路上堵车，他们仍在仪式开始前赶到。

examples.en: The neighbours built a spite fence right along the property line.
examples.cn: 邻居们紧贴地界修了一道赌气栅栏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯派特」——不为好处只为看塔倒：恶意；不顾

root: spite 经古法语 despit「轻蔑」追溯至拉丁语 despicere「俯视」，由 de-「向下」加 specere「看」构成；一般认为印欧词根 *spei- 表示「指向、尖」，更早来源不确定。despite 与 despise 同属这一「往下看」词族。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spite run from the push of malice to the wall that gets walked past: hurting, grudging, defying, and outlasting.
sensesIntro.cn: spite 的义项从恶意的一推延展到被绕过的墙：伤人、怀怨、违抗与坚持。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that topples a tower only to watch it fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手推倒塔，只为看它倒塌。

branches.en: THE MALICE LINE: the push and the grudge that feeds it.
branches.cn: 恶意线：那一推，以及喂养它的旧怨。

branches.en: THE DESPITE LINE: the wall stands, the deed goes on anyway.
branches.cn: in spite of 线：墙立着，事照做。

branches.en: THE VERB LINE: the push itself gets a verb of its own.
branches.cn: 动词线：推搡动作自成动词。

branches.en: THE WARNING LINE: old sayings show spite turning on itself.
branches.cn: 警示线：古谚展示恶意反噬自身。

branches.en: THE BUILT GRUDGE LINE: fences carry spite, and old poems wear defiance.
branches.cn: 成形的怨恨线：栅栏承载恶意，旧诗披挂轻蔑。

intro.en: Spite was clipped from despite, and English builds on it with plain suffixes.
intro.cn: spite 由 despite 截短而来；英语用朴素后缀在其上构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin despicere and Old French despit are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 despicere 与古法语 despit 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the distant parent.

items.exampleCN: 这个名词给出英语 despite。

items.example: The short form split off in the thirteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 短形式于十三世纪分出。
它构成 despite 与 despise。

items.example: The seeing verb anchors the family.
It keeps the looking-down sense plainly.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「怀恶意的；恶毒的」
由 spiteful 加副词后缀构成，义为「恶毒地」
由 spiteful 加名词后缀构成，义为「恶毒；怨恨」
同源词，义为「尽管；不顾」

definition_zh: 劈开；分裂；分担；绝交；（名）裂缝；分歧
definition_en: to divide something into two or more parts by force or along a line, or a division
core_image: 一把斧头落在木头正中，年轮从裂缝向两侧展开
scene: 木场的圆木架上横着一段粗木。The woodcutter split the log with a single clean stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 split 是「劈开」（第 1 个义项：沿一线用力分成两半）；句意为伐木工一斧利落劈开圆木。图中可辨识物件：圆木、斧头、木架。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「劈裂者；分裂者」
由动词现在分词作形容词，义为「剧烈的（头痛）；裂开的」
同义借词，义为「分叉」（书面）
近义借词，义为「（组织）分裂」

senses.title: To divide by force along a line
senses.definition: to break or divide something into parts, especially along a grain or seam
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成数块，尤指沿纹理或接缝
senses.example: The axe split the log down the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 斧头把圆木从中间劈开。
senses.why: One stroke follows the hidden line the wood already holds.
senses.whyCN: 一斧顺着木头里早已藏着的线落下。

senses.title: To divide into groups or parts
senses.definition: to divide into smaller groups or parts, especially by disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 分成更小的群体或部分，尤指因分歧
senses.example: The party split into two camps over the tax plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该党因税制方案分裂为两大阵营。
senses.why: The wood image lifts off the table: people, like grain, part along a line of strain.
senses.whyCN: 木材意象离开桌面：人群像木纹一样沿受力线分开。

senses.title: To share and divide up
senses.definition: to divide something such as money or work between people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们之间分摊钱物或工作
senses.example: We agreed to split the cost of the taxi.
senses.exampleCN: 我们说好平摊出租车费。
senses.why: Once something is divided, each piece belongs to someone.
senses.whyCN: 一经分开，每一份都有了归属。

senses.title: To end a relationship
senses.definition: to end a friendship, partnership, or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 结束友谊、合伙或婚姻
senses.example: The two founders split last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 两位创始人去年春天散伙了。
senses.why: The seam that held two things together finally gives way.
senses.whyCN: 维系两者的接缝最终崩开。

senses.title: A crack or tear
senses.definition: a crack or lengthwise tear in something
senses.definitionCN: 物体上的裂缝或纵向破口
senses.example: There is a long split in the old door panel.
senses.exampleCN: 旧门板上有一道长长的裂缝。
senses.why: The verb hardens into a noun: the line left by the blow is named.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝为名词：一击留下的线被命名。

senses.title: A division of opinion
senses.definition: a division or disagreement between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体间的分歧
senses.example: The vote revealed a deep split in the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 投票暴露了委员会内部的深刻分歧。
senses.why: The hidden grain of a group shows itself as a crack of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 群体隐秘的纹理以意见的裂缝显形。

senses.title: A share or portion
senses.definition: a part of a profit or sum that someone receives
senses.definitionCN: 利润或款项中某人所得的一份
senses.example: She took her split of the prize money.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿走了属于自己的一份奖金。
senses.why: Each half of the wood carries away its own weight.
senses.whyCN: 劈开的一半带走属于它自己的分量。

senses.title: Split second: a tiny moment
senses.definition: a very brief moment of time, as in a split second
senses.definitionCN: 极短的片刻，如一刹那
senses.example: The goalkeeper reacted in a split second.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员在一刹那间作出反应。
senses.why: Time itself can be divided, one hairline crack wide.
senses.whyCN: 时间本身也能被劈开，裂口只有发丝宽。

intro.en: Split is a native English verb of the axe and the seam, with relatives across the Germanic sea.
intro.cn: split 是斧头与接缝世界的本土英语动词，在海对岸的日耳曼语里有亲族。

items.en: *splīdan- is generally reconstructed as "to split, cleave"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *splīdan- 表示「劈开、裂开」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Dutch splitten and related Low German forms kept the same splitting image.
items.cn: 荷兰语 splitten 与相关低地德语形式保留了同样的劈裂意象。

items.en: The verb entered standard English in the sixteenth century from northern and maritime use.
items.cn: 该动词于十六世纪经北部及海上用法进入标准英语。

items.en: Some sources link it to Middle English splenten "to split wood", of the same Low German family.
items.cn: 一些辞源将其与中古英语 splenten「劈木」相联，同属低地德语词族。

items.en: The word now serves wood, groups, bills, hair and even time.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词服务于木头、群体、账单、头发乃至时间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of dividing.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收表示分开的动词。

entries.definition: One who or something that splits, or a device for dividing signals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指劈裂者或信号分配器。

entries.definition: British past of spill; one letter apart and a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: spill 的英式过去式；仅一字母之差，属另一个动词。

entries.definition: A narrow cut; shares the cutting image but has its own word history.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「切缝」；同属切割意象但词史独立。

entries.definition: A small quarrel or the past of spit; letters shuffled and of different line.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「小争吵」或 spit 的过去式；字母换位，词系不同。

entries.definition: Liquid scattering; begins like split but has another root.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「泼溅」；起首与 split 相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: The general word for separating into parts, without force implied.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体分开的通用词，不暗含强力。

entries.definition: A literary verb to split along a natural line.
entries.definitionCN: 书面动词，指沿自然纹路劈开。

entries.definition: To break with a sharp sound, often partly.
entries.definitionCN: 带着脆响裂开，常未断尽。

entries.definition: To cut off completely, especially a connection.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底切断，尤指关系。

entries.definition: A sudden breaking apart, formal or medical.
entries.definitionCN: 骤然破裂，正式或医学用语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the axe image and the split forms the word really takes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用斧头意象，以及该词真实呈现的 split 形式。

normal.en: The verb never changes its clothes: split, split, split for past and participle.
normal.cn: 这个动词从不换装：过去式与过去分词都是 split。

normal.en: Split the bill is what friends say when sharing the cost.
normal.cn: 朋友分摊花销时说的是 split the bill。

normal.en: Split up can mean two people ending their relationship.
normal.cn: split up 可指两人结束关系。

normal.en: A split second is time cut as thin as a wood chip.
normal.cn: split second 是被劈得薄如木屑的一瞬。

normal.en: Splitting headache feels like the head itself has been cleaved.
normal.cn: splitting headache 感觉像头被劈开。

abstract.en: Picture the axe resting exactly on the line the grain drew long ago.
abstract.cn: 想象斧头恰好落在木纹早已画好的那道线上。

abstract.en: When a group splits, invisible grain becomes a visible crack.
abstract.cn: 群体分裂时，看不见的纹理变成看得见的裂缝。

abstract.en: Every split leaves two halves, and each half remembers being whole.
abstract.cn: 每次劈开都留下两半，而每一半都记得曾经的完整。

examples.en: They split the logs and stacked them by the shed.
examples.cn: 他们劈好木柴，堆在小屋旁。

examples.en: The committee split evenly on the proposal, six votes each way.
examples.cn: 委员会对该提案的表决正好五五开。

examples.en: Let us split the difference and each pay twenty.
examples.cn: 我们各让一步，每人付二十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯普利特」——一斧顺着木纹落下：劈开；分裂

root: split 属日耳曼语源，一般认为原始日耳曼语 *splīdan- 表示「劈开」，与荷兰语 splitten 同族；经中古英语与北部、海上用法于十六世纪进入标准英语，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of split follow one axe stroke from wood to people to time: cleaving, dividing, sharing, and parting.
sensesIntro.cn: split 的义项随一斧落下，从木头走到人群再走到时间：劈裂、分化、分摊与分离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axe falling along the line the wood has always held.
core.cn: 核心意象：一斧顺着木头一直藏着的那道线落下。

branches.en: THE WOOD LINE: force follows the hidden seam and things come apart.
branches.cn: 木材线：强力顺着暗缝，物体分开。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE LINE: groups crack along their own grain into camps and opinions.
branches.cn: 人群线：群体沿自身纹理裂为阵营与分歧。

branches.en: THE FAIR LINE: once divided, every piece has an owner.
branches.cn: 公平线：一经分开，每份各有其主。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: even a moment can be split hairline-thin.
branches.cn: 时钟线：连一瞬也能被劈成发丝宽。

branches.en: THE BREAKING-AWAY LINE: seams give way and partnerships end.
branches.cn: 决裂线：接缝崩开，伙伴散伙。

intro.en: Split is a bare Germanic root; English adds only its own small endings around it.
intro.cn: split 是裸的日耳曼词根；英语只在它周围加自家的小词尾。

latinIntro.en: Split is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: split 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: The Dutch verb is a close relative.
It gives splitting with doubled t.
items.exampleCN: 双写 t 构成 splitting。
这个复合词把时间也劈开。

items.example: The dessert is named for its divided fruit.
items.exampleCN: 该甜品以剖开的香蕉命名。

items.example: The hair cracks like wood grain.

definition_zh: 破坏；糟蹋；宠坏；变质；（名）战利品；赃物
definition_en: to harm or ruin something, or goods taken by force in war
core_image: 一颗好苹果在篮子里慢慢烂开，褐斑一圈圈扩大
scene: 野餐垫上摆着装水果的篮子。The hot sun spoiled the fruit before lunch even started.
sceneCN: 这里 spoil 是「使变质、毁坏」（第 1 个义项：损坏食物或事物）；句意为烈日在午餐开始前就把水果晒坏了。图中可辨识物件：野餐垫、水果篮、日光。

pos.zh: 动词：破坏；糟蹋；宠坏；变质

collocations.phrase: spare the rod and spoil the child

derivatives.zh: 英式过去分词作形容词，义为「被宠坏的；变质的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「剧透；破坏者」
由 de- 加本词构成，义为「掠夺；蹂躏」（书面）
同 spoliation，义为「掠夺」

senses.title: To ruin or damage something
senses.definition: to harm or reduce the value or quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 损害或降低某物的价值与品质
senses.example: One loud engine spoiled the quiet of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一声轰鸣的发动机毁掉了山谷的宁静。
senses.why: The good thing rots from the point where force or neglect touches it.
senses.whyCN: 好物从强力或疏忽触碰之点开始腐烂。

senses.title: To make food unfit to eat
senses.definition: to make food or perishable goods go bad
senses.definitionCN: 使食物或易腐物品变坏
senses.example: The milk spoiled overnight in the warm kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶在温暖的厨房里一夜之间变质了。
senses.why: What was stored for later is taken by decay now.
senses.whyCN: 为以后存的口粮，此刻被腐坏夺走。

senses.title: To treat a child too indulgently
senses.definition: to give a child too much of what it wants, so it behaves badly
senses.definitionCN: 对孩子有求必应，致其任性
senses.example: Grandparents spoiled the twins with sweets and late nights.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父母用糖果和熬夜把双胞胎宠坏了。
senses.why: Too much sweetness is itself a kind of ruin.
senses.whyCN: 过多的甜本身就是一种毁坏。

senses.title: To rob or plunder
senses.definition: to take goods by force, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 以强力夺取财物，旧用法
senses.example: The raiders spoiled the granaries of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 劫掠者抢走了村庄的谷仓。
senses.why: Before the ruin sense, the taking of goods was the core.
senses.whyCN: 在毁坏义之前，夺取财物才是核心。

senses.title: Spoils: goods taken in war
senses.definition: goods or property seized by the victors in a war
senses.definitionCN: 战争胜利者夺取的财物
senses.example: The victors divided the spoils of the captured city.
senses.exampleCN: 胜利者瓜分了攻陷城池的战利品。
senses.why: What war ruins on one side becomes gain on the other.
senses.whyCN: 战争毁掉一方的，成了另一方的所得。

senses.title: Spoils: profits of an enterprise
senses.definition: benefits or profits gained from an activity, as in share the spoils
senses.definitionCN: 从活动中获得的好处，如分赃之说
senses.example: The two firms agreed to share the spoils of the new market.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司约定瓜分新市场的收益。
senses.why: Plunder grows a business suit: gain taken from a contest.
senses.whyCN: 掠夺换上西装：从竞争中夺取的收益。

senses.title: To weaken a vote by marking it wrongly
senses.definition: to mark a ballot wrongly so that it cannot be counted
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上误填使其无法计入
senses.example: He spoiled his ballot by writing on it twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他在选票上写了两处，使其作废。
senses.why: A ruined paper ruins the choice it carried.
senses.whyCN: 被毁的纸毁掉了它所承载的选择。

senses.title: To spoil for: to eager for a fight
senses.definition: to have a strong desire for a fight or contest
senses.definitionCN: 极欲争斗或较量
senses.example: The young player was spoiling for a rematch.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员憋着一股劲要重赛一场。
senses.why: The ruined mood turns restless, hunting for an outlet.
senses.whyCN: 被搅坏的心气不得安宁，四处寻衅。

intro.en: Spoil is a Latin plunder-word that drifted from taking goods to ruining them.
intro.cn: spoil 是拉丁语的掠夺词，从夺取财物漂移为毁坏财物。

items.en: *spel- is generally reconstructed as "to split off, break off"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spel- 表示「剥落、掰下」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin spoliare meant "to strip of skin or goods, to plunder", from spolium "skin, hide taken from prey".
items.cn: 拉丁语 spoliare 意为「剥取皮毛、掠夺」，出自 spolium「猎物之皮」。

items.en: Late Latin spoiliare passed into Old French espoillier with the plundering sense.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 spoiliare 经古法语 espoillier 保留掠夺义。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century as a verb of plunder.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪收下该词，作掠夺动词。

items.en: The sense shifted to ruining and spoiling, while spoils kept the plunder meaning.
items.cn: 词义转向毁坏与糟蹋，而 spoils 保留掠夺义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plunder family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words of ruining and loot.
note.cn: 形近组收掠夺词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示毁坏与赃物的词。

entries.definition: British past form, also an adjective for pampered children.
entries.definitionCN: 英式过去式，也作形容词形容被宠坏的孩子。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to strip a place of its wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，义为「掠夺一地之财」。

entries.definition: A legal term for the destruction or plundering of property.
entries.definitionCN: 法律术语，指财产的毁损或掠夺。

entries.definition: Earth or to stain; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「土壤；弄脏」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: Something that spoils, or a plot detail given away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指破坏者或被剧透的情节。

entries.definition: To destroy completely, stronger and more final than spoil.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底摧毁，比 spoil 更强、更不可逆。

entries.definition: To smash and destroy, often of physical things.
entries.definitionCN: 砸毁、破坏，多用于实物。

entries.definition: To take goods by force, matching the old spoils sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以强力夺取财物，对应 spoils 旧义。

entries.definition: To impair the perfection of something, lighter than ruin.
entries.definitionCN: 损害某物的完美，程度轻于 ruin。

entries.definition: To indulge someone, matching the spoilt-child sense.
entries.definitionCN: 纵容、娇惯，对应宠坏义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the apple image and the plunder history the word really has.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用烂苹果意象，以及该词真实的掠夺史。

normal.en: Latin spolium was the skin stripped from prey: taking came first.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 spolium 是从猎物剥下的皮：先有夺取。

normal.en: The spoils of war are what the victors take home.
normal.cn: spoils of war 是胜利者带回家的东西。

normal.en: Spoilt food and spoilt children both got too much of something.
normal.cn: 变质的食物与被宠坏的孩子，都是「得了太多」。

normal.en: Spoiled with an -ed is American; spoilt with a -t is British.
normal.cn: -ed 的 spoiled 是美式，-t 的 spoilt 是英式。

normal.en: Spoiler alert: the warning that a plot will be spoiled.
normal.cn: spoiler alert：提醒剧情即将被「剧透」毁掉。

abstract.en: Brown spots spread one ring at a time: ruin rarely happens all at once.
abstract.cn: 褐斑一圈圈扩大：毁坏很少一瞬完成。

abstract.en: Too much sugar keeps the apple sweet and rots it early.
abstract.cn: 过多的糖让苹果保持甜，也提前把它催烂。

abstract.en: The basket is a small kingdom: whatever the strong take from it, the rest spoils.
abstract.cn: 篮子是个小王国：强者取走多少，剩下的就烂多少。

examples.en: Heavy rain spoiled the whole afternoon at the beach.
examples.cn: 大雨毁掉了海滩上整整一个下午。

examples.en: The meat will spoil if the fridge stops running.
examples.cn: 冰箱一停，肉就会变质。

examples.en: Winners once divided the spoils openly among the crew.
examples.cn: 从前胜利者会在船员间公开分赃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯波伊尔」——好苹果一圈圈烂开：毁坏；战利品

root: spoil 经古法语 espoillier「掠夺」追溯至拉丁语 spoliare「剥取、劫掠」，出自 spolium「猎物之皮」；一般认为印欧词根 *spel- 表示「剥落」，更早来源不确定。despoil、spoliation 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spoil move from taking to ruining: plunder first, then decay, indulgence, and the profits of a contest.
sensesIntro.cn: spoil 的义项从夺取走向毁坏：先是掠夺，继而是腐坏、溺爱与竞争所得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a good apple spreading brown rings inside the basket.
core.cn: 核心意象：篮中一颗好苹果，褐斑一圈圈扩散。

branches.en: THE ROT LINE: neglect, warmth or too much sweetness ruins the good thing.
branches.cn: 腐烂线：疏忽、温热或过量甜分毁掉好物。

branches.en: THE PLUNDER LINE: the oldest sense takes goods by force.
branches.cn: 掠夺线：最古老的义以强力夺财。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS LINE: contest profits wear the old plunder word.
branches.cn: 商业线：竞争所得披着旧的掠夺词。

branches.en: THE BALLOT LINE: one ruined paper ruins one vote.
branches.cn: 选票线：一张废纸毁掉一票。

branches.en: THE FIGHT LINE: a spoilt mood hunts for a contest.
branches.cn: 寻衅线：被搅坏的心气渴望较量。

intro.en: Spoil keeps its Latin plunder stem visible, and English adds simple endings.
intro.cn: spoil 的拉丁掠夺词干清晰可见；英语只加简单词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin spoliare and Old French espoillier are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spoliare 与古法语 espoillier 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.example: The noun is the seed of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的种子。

items.example: The verb passed into French and English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入法语与英语。

items.example: It carried the word into English.

items.exampleCN: 英式英语用 -t 构成 spoilt。

items.example: It keeps the Latin shape intact.
The plural keeps the plunder sense.

由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「剧透；破坏者」
由 de- 加本词构成，义为「掠夺；蹂躏」（书面）
同 spoliation，义为「掠夺」

definition_zh: 发言人；代言人
definition_en: a person chosen to speak officially for a group, organization, or another person
core_image: 一排话筒前的人：身后组织的所有话，都从他嘴里出来
scene: 新闻发布厅里闪光灯亮成一片。The company spokesman read a short statement to the reporters.
sceneCN: 这里 spokesman 是「发言人」（第 1 个义项：代表组织正式发言者）；句意为公司发言人向记者宣读了一份简短声明。图中可辨识物件：话筒、发布会讲台、闪光灯。

derivatives.zh: 同词构词的阴性形式，义为「女发言人」
中性化形式，义为「发言人（不区分性别）」
本词复数形式
构词基础动词，义为「说话」

senses.title: One who speaks for a group
senses.definition: a person selected to make statements on behalf of others
senses.definitionCN: 被选定代表他人发声的人
senses.example: A union spokesman answered the pay questions.
senses.exampleCN: 工会发言人回答了薪酬问题。
senses.why: One mouth is placed before many: the crowd's words travel through a single throat.
senses.whyCN: 一张嘴被放在众人之前：人群的话经由一副喉咙说出。

senses.title: An official media contact
senses.definition: the designated contact who gives statements to journalists
senses.definitionCN: 被指定向记者发布声明的人
senses.example: The ministry spokesman confirmed the date of the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 部委发言人确认了会谈日期。
senses.why: The office builds a wall of process, and the spokesman is its speaking gate.
senses.whyCN: 机关筑起程序的墙，发言人是墙上那道会说话的门。

senses.title: Spokesman or spokesperson usage
senses.titleCN: spokesman 与 spokesperson 的用法
senses.definition: spokesman is traditional; spokesperson avoids marking gender
senses.definitionCN: spokesman 是传统形式；spokesperson 不标性别
senses.example: The press office now prefers the term spokesperson.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻办公室现在更倾向用 spokesperson 一词。
senses.why: Language remodels the old compound to fit the modern crowd.
senses.whyCN: 语言改造旧复合词以适应现代人群。

senses.title: In history: one who speaks up for a cause
senses.definition: a person who speaks up for a cause or movement
senses.definitionCN: 为某事业或运动公开发声的人
senses.example: The movement found its spokesman in a young lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动在一位年轻律师身上找到了代言人。
senses.why: A cause without a voice stays invisible; one speaker makes it seen.
senses.whyCN: 无声的事业无影无形；一个发声者让它显形。

senses.title: The genitive line: spokes of speech
senses.titleCN: 构词里的属格：说话之口
senses.definition: the word contains an old genitive: one man of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 该词含有古老的属格：属于「说话」的那个人
senses.example: The -s in spokesman is an old possessive, like in statesman.
senses.exampleCN: spokesman 中的 -s 是古老的属格标记，如 statesman 中的用法。
senses.why: Old English grammar hides inside the compound like a fossil in stone.
senses.whyCN: 古英语语法像石中化石一样藏在复合词里。

senses.title: Spokes as radiating lines
senses.definition: the nouns spoke (wheel bar) and spokesman share nothing historically, yet the wheel image helps memory
senses.definitionCN: spoke（轮辐）与 spokesman 词源无关，但轮辐意象有助记忆
senses.example: Like the spokes of a wheel, every statement runs from the centre through him.
senses.exampleCN: 如轮辐一般，每条声明都从中心经由他发出。
senses.why: The image is a memory aid only, not a real relative.
senses.whyCN: 这只是记忆辅助，并非真正的亲族。

senses.title: A spokesman against something
senses.definition: one who officially voices opposition for others
senses.definitionCN: 代表众人正式表达反对的人
senses.example: She acted as spokesman for the objecting residents.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任反对居民们的代言人。
senses.why: The gate swings both ways: it can carry refusal as well as approval.
senses.whyCN: 这扇门双向开合：既承载赞成，也承载拒绝。

senses.title: Figurative: the face of a thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that symbolically represents an organization
senses.definitionCN: 象征性地代表某组织的人或物
senses.example: The veteran captain became the team's public spokesman.
senses.exampleCN: 老队长成了球队的公众门面。
senses.why: When a face is needed, the crowd picks the steadiest one.
senses.whyCN: 需要一张脸时，人群会挑最稳的那一张。

intro.en: Spokesman is an English compound with an old grammar fossil inside it.
intro.cn: spokesman 是英语复合词，内部藏着一枚古语法的化石。

items.en: Old English genitive speca meant "of speech", a possessive form of spec "speech".
items.cn: 古英语属格 speca 意为「言语的」，是 spec「言语」的所有格形式。

items.en: Compounds like spokesman and statesman keep this old genitive -s.
items.cn: spokesman、statesman 等复合词保留了这一古老的属格 -s。

items.en: Middle English spoke(s)man meant "one who speaks for another".
items.cn: 中古英语 spoke(s)man 意为「代他人发言者」。

items.en: The modern word settled in the seventeenth century for official representatives.
items.cn: 现代形式于十七世纪定型，指官方代表。

items.en: Spokeswoman and spokesperson arose in the twentieth century for inclusive usage.
items.cn: spokeswoman 与 spokesperson 产生于二十世纪，以实现无性别指向的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the speaking family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for representation.
note.cn: 形近组收「说话」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示代表身份的词。

entries.definition: The female form of spokesman.
entries.definitionCN: spokesman 的阴性形式。

entries.definition: The gender-neutral form now widely preferred.
entries.definitionCN: 如今被广泛使用的中性形式。

entries.definition: The plural of spokesman.
entries.definitionCN: spokesman 的复数形式。

entries.definition: A wheel bar or the past of speak; unrelated in the spokesman compound.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「轮辐」或 speak 的过去式；与复合词中的属格 -s 无关。

entries.definition: Plural of spoke; merely looks like the genitive inside the compound.
entries.definitionCN: spoke 的复数；只是与复合词内的属格形似。

entries.definition: One who acts or votes for others, broader than speaking only.
entries.definitionCN: 代他人行事或投票者，范围比仅发言更广。

entries.definition: One sent to act for others, often at meetings.
entries.definitionCN: 被派遣代表他人者，多指会议场合。

entries.definition: An informal, often critical word for one who relays another's views.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式且常含贬义，指传声筒。

entries.definition: An official messenger sent between governments.
entries.definitionCN: 政府间派出的正式使者。

entries.definition: One who pleads a cause publicly for others.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人公开申辩、鼓吹者。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the compound structure and the wheel image the word invites.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用复合词结构，以及该词引发的轮辐意象。

normal.en: spokes + man: the -s is an old genitive, "the man of speaking".
normal.cn: spokes + man：-s 是古老属格，即「属于说话的人」。

normal.en: Statesman hides the same fossil: the man of the state.
normal.cn: statesman 藏着同一化石：「属于国家的人」。

normal.en: A spokesman for the company speaks with the company's voice.
normal.cn: 公司发言人以公司的声音说话。

normal.en: The neutral word spokesperson avoids marking gender.
normal.cn: 中性词 spokesperson 不标记性别。

normal.en: Picture every wheel spoke running from the hub through one rim point.
normal.cn: 想象每根轮辐都从轴心通向轮缘同一点。

abstract.en: One mouth at the microphone, a hundred silent mouths behind it.
abstract.cn: 话筒前一张嘴，身后一百张沉默的嘴。

abstract.en: The hub speaks only through the spokes it has chosen.
abstract.cn: 轴心只通过它选定的轮辐说话。

abstract.en: When the compound grows a W or a PERSON, the gate widens for all.
abstract.cn: 复合词长出 W 或 PERSON，那扇门就向所有人敞开。

examples.en: A police spokesman said the investigation was continuing.
examples.cn: 警方发言人表示调查仍在进行。

examples.en: The union spokesman rejected the pay offer on live television.
examples.cn: 工会发言人在电视直播中拒绝了薪酬方案。

examples.en: She served as spokesman for the residents against the building plan.
examples.cn: 她担任反对建筑方案的居民代言人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯波克斯曼」——话筒前的一张嘴替众人开口：发言人

root: spokesman 由古英语属格 speca「言语的」加 man 构成，即「属于言语的人」；该属格 -s 亦见于 statesman；复合形式定型于近代英语。现代英语另造 spokeswoman 与 spokesperson。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spokesman all put one mouth before many: official contact, cause-speaker, and the grammar fossil inside the compound.
sensesIntro.cn: spokesman 的义项都把一张嘴放在众人之前：官方联络、事业发声者，以及复合词内的语法化石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one microphone in front, a whole organization speaking through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：面前一支话筒，整个组织的话经它说出。

branches.en: THE GATE LINE: the crowd's words pass through one official mouth.
branches.cn: 门线：人群的话语经由一张官方之口。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR LINE: the old genitive -s hides in the compound.
branches.cn: 语法线：古老属格 -s 藏在复合词中。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: the gate swings for approval and refusal alike.
branches.cn: 事业线：这扇门为赞成与反对同样开合。

branches.en: THE WHEEL LINE: statements radiate like spokes from a hub.
branches.cn: 轮辐线：声明如辐条自轴心放射。

branches.en: THE MODERN LINE: spokesperson widens the gate; a team picks its steadiest face.
branches.cn: 现代线：spokesperson 拓宽门径；团队选出最稳的门面。

intro.en: Spokesman is a self-built English compound; its parts are speech and person.
intro.cn: spokesman 是英语自建的复合词；构件就是「言语」与「人」。

latinIntro.en: Spokesman is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Old English genitive is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: spokesman 属日耳曼语源，拉丁同源词列表为空；古英语属格形式有文献记录。

items.exampleCN: 化石级属格藏在复合词内。

items.exampleCN: 它构成复合词的「人」半边。
它以 woman 替换 man。
它以 person 替换 man。

items.example: Another genitive compound of the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 同模式的另一属格复合词。

items.example: The plural turns man into men.
items.exampleCN: 复数把 man 变为 men。

items.example: The living verb of the same family.

items.exampleCN: 它在复合词内标记领属。

definition_zh: 匙；勺；一勺的量；（动）拥抱（spoon）
definition_en: a tool with a shallow bowl and a handle used for eating, stirring, or serving food
core_image: 一柄圆头小勺静静躺在糖罐边，勺窝里盛着半勺白糖
scene: 清晨的厨房里，茶杯还冒着热气。She stirred her tea slowly with a silver spoon.
sceneCN: 这里 spoon 是「匙、勺」（第 1 个义项：带柄浅窝的餐具）；句意为她用银勺慢慢搅茶。图中可辨识物件：茶杯、银勺、糖罐。

pos.zh: 动词：用勺舀；（旧）相拥而卧

collocations.phrase: born with a silver spoon in one's mouth

derivatives.zh: 由本词加量后缀构成，义为「一勺之量」
复合词，义为「琵鹭（嘴如匙）」
人名衍生词，义为「首音互换（斯普纳现象）」
复合词，义为「汤匙（量具）」

senses.title: A utensil for eating or stirring
senses.definition: a utensil with a small shallow bowl on a handle, used for eating or stirring
senses.definitionCN: 柄端带浅窝的餐具，用于进食或搅拌
senses.example: The baby learned to hold a spoon by herself.
senses.exampleCN: 宝宝学会了自己拿勺。
senses.why: A tiny bowl on a stick: the simplest vessel ever fitted to a hand.
senses.whyCN: 小棍上的小窝：最简的容器恰好配上手掌。

senses.title: A measured amount a spoon holds
senses.definition: an amount that a spoon holds, used as a rough measure
senses.definitionCN: 一勺所容之量，用作粗略计量
senses.example: Add one spoon of honey to the warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 在温水里加一勺蜂蜜。
senses.why: The bowl itself becomes the scale for kitchen and medicine.
senses.whyCN: 勺窝本身成了厨房与药房的天平。

senses.title: To lift or move with a spoon
senses.definition: to lift or transfer something with or as if with a spoon
senses.definitionCN: 用勺或如用勺般舀起
senses.example: She spooned soup into the small bowls.
senses.exampleCN: 她把汤舀进小碗里。
senses.why: The tool lends its motion to the hand that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 工具把它的动作借给握它的手。

senses.title: Wooden spoon: last place
senses.definition: a mock prize for finishing last in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中垫底的搞笑奖项
senses.example: The losing team collected their wooden spoon with laughs.
senses.exampleCN: 垫底的队伍笑着领走了他们的木勺奖。
senses.why: In old rowing, the slowest crew once won a literal wooden spoon.
senses.whyCN: 旧时赛艇最慢的队伍真的得到一把木勺。

senses.title: Born with a silver spoon
senses.definition: to be born into wealth, as in born with a silver spoon in one's mouth
senses.definitionCN: 生于富裕家庭，如「含着银勺出生」
senses.example: He was born with a silver spoon in his mouth and never learned to scrimp.
senses.exampleCN: 他生于富贵之家，从不知节俭。
senses.why: Christening gifts once included spoons: wealth served from the first day.
senses.whyCN: 旧时受洗礼会赠勺：财富从第一天起就「喂」到嘴里。

senses.title: To cuddle side by side
senses.definition: to lie closely against a partner, both facing the same way, in slang
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指两人朝同一方向贴身而卧
senses.example: The old song told of spooning on the porch swing.
senses.exampleCN: 老歌唱的是 porch swing 上相拥。
senses.why: Two spoons nest in the drawer the way two people nest.
senses.whyCN: 抽屉里两把勺相叠，恰如两人相偎。

senses.title: Spoon-fed: given everything
senses.definition: given answers or care in a way that prevents independence
senses.definitionCN: 被喂给答案或照料，以致无法独立
senses.example: The students resented being spoon-fed formulas.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们反感被填鸭式灌输公式。
senses.why: What is placed directly in the mouth never learns to seek.
senses.whyCN: 直接送进嘴里的东西，从不学会自己寻找。

senses.title: A spoonerism echo
senses.definition: spoonerism, named after a dean, refers to swapped word beginnings
senses.definitionCN: spoonerism 以院长之姓命名，指词首字母互换
senses.example: The classic spoonerism turns loving shepherd into shoving leopard.
senses.exampleCN: 经典 spoonerism 把 loving shepherd 说成 shoving leopard。
senses.why: A family of words gathered around one scholar's slip.
senses.whyCN: 一词族因一位学者的口误而聚拢。

intro.en: Spoon began as a chip of wood and grew into the polished vessel on the table.
intro.cn: spoon 起于一片木头刨片，最终长成餐桌上的精致器皿。

items.en: *spōnō is generally reconstructed as "a chip, splinter of wood"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spōnō 表示「木片、刨花」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spon meant "a chip, a shaving of wood", later a wooden eating utensil.
items.cn: 古英语 spon 意为「木片、刨花」，后指木质食器。

items.en: Old Norse spoon "a spoon" reinforced or reshaped the English form.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 spoon「勺」强化或重塑了英语形式。

items.en: The word settled on the eating vessel as wood gave way to horn, pewter and silver.
items.cn: 中古英语中，随着木制让位于角、锡与银，词义固定于食器。

items.en: The word now serves meals, measures, idioms and even a mating verb in slang.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词服务于饮食、计量、习语，俚语中甚至作动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers eating tools.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收进食器具。

entries.definition: The amount a spoon can hold.
entries.definitionCN: 一勺所容之量。

entries.definition: A wading bird with a spoon-shaped bill.
entries.definitionCN: 嘴形如勺的涉禽，琵鹭。

entries.definition: A swap of word beginnings, named after Dean Spooner.
entries.definitionCN: 词首互换现象，以斯普纳院长命名。

entries.definition: A reel for thread; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「线轴」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: A hoax or parody; merely sounds alike and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「戏仿、骗局」；仅读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A large deep spoon for serving soup.
entries.definitionCN: 舀汤用的深柄大勺。

entries.definition: A pronged eating tool that spears instead of scooping.
entries.definitionCN: 带齿餐具，用于叉取而非舀取。

entries.definition: A curved tool for lifting loose material.
entries.definitionCN: 舀取散物的弯形工具。

entries.definition: A larger spoon, also a unit of measure.
entries.definitionCN: 较大的勺，也作计量单位。

entries.definition: A small spoon, also a unit of measure.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的勺，也作计量单位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chip-of-wood origin and the idioms the word really lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用「木片」词源与该词真实所在的习语。

normal.en: Old English spon was just a chip of wood: the first spoons were carved, not cast.
normal.cn: 古英语 spon 只是木片：最早的勺是刨出来的，不是铸出来的。

normal.en: Born with a silver spoon means born rich.
normal.cn: born with a silver spoon 意为生于富贵。

normal.en: The wooden spoon goes to the team that finishes last.
normal.cn: wooden spoon 归垫底的队伍。

normal.en: One spoon of sugar is the smallest recipe in the kitchen.
normal.cn: 一勺糖是厨房里最小的「菜谱」。

normal.en: Spooned soup, spooned honey: the verb keeps the tool's motion.
normal.cn: 舀汤舀蜜：动词保留了工具的动作。

abstract.en: Picture the first spoon: a flat chip curved by a knife in one evening.
abstract.cn: 想象第一把勺：一个晚上用刀弯出的一片木。

abstract.en: The bowl on the handle measures as it serves: tool and scale in one.
abstract.cn: 柄上的小窝一边盛取一边计量：工具与天平合一。

abstract.en: Two spoons in a drawer lie nested like sleeping people.
abstract.cn: 抽屉里两把勺相叠而卧，如相拥而眠的人。

examples.en: She set a clean spoon beside each plate.
examples.cn: 她在每个餐盘旁摆了一把干净的勺子。

examples.en: Take two spoons of the syrup after every meal.
examples.cn: 每餐后服用两勺糖浆。

examples.en: The runner-up team joked about the wooden spoon they earned.
examples.cn: 亚军队调侃他们「赢得」的末位木勺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯普恩」——木片刨出的小窝：匙；一勺之量

root: spoon 属日耳曼语源，古英语 spon 意为「木片、刨花」，古诺斯语 spoon「勺」与之相关，一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spōnō 表示「木片」，更早来源不确定。后由「木制食器」固定为今天的「匙」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spoon move from the carved chip to the silver vessel: eating tool, measure, motion, and the idioms of wealth and last place.
sensesIntro.cn: spoon 的义项从刨片走向银器：食具、计量、动作，以及富贵与末位的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shallow bowl on a handle, resting by the sugar jar.
core.cn: 核心意象：柄端一只浅窝，静静靠着糖罐。

branches.en: THE TOOL LINE: the chip carved into a vessel and its motion.
branches.cn: 工具线：木片凿成器皿，器皿赋予动作。

branches.en: THE MEASURE LINE: the bowl doubles as a scale.
branches.cn: 计量线：勺窝兼任天平。

branches.en: THE LAST-PLACE LINE: the slowest crew once won a real wooden spoon.
branches.cn: 末位线：最慢的船队真得过一把木勺。

branches.en: THE WEALTH LINE: christening spoons served riches from day one.
branches.cn: 富贵线：受洗赠勺，财富自第一天喂起。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: nesting spoons, spoon-fed students, and one dean's famous slip.
branches.cn: 词族线：相叠的勺、被填喂的学生与一位院长的著名口误。

intro.en: Spoon is a bare Germanic noun; compounds and the measure suffix -ful grow beside it.
intro.cn: spoon 是裸的日耳曼名词；复合词与量词后缀 -ful 在它旁边生长。

latinIntro.en: Spoon is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: spoon 属日耳曼语源，拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
The participle keeps the nesting image.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式保留相叠意象。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加量后缀构成，义为「一勺之量」
复合词，义为「琵鹭（嘴如匙）」
人名衍生词，义为「首音互换（斯普纳现象）」
复合词，义为「汤匙（量具）」

definition_zh: 体育运动；比赛；乐趣；（古）嬉戏；（生）变种
definition_en: a game or physical activity involving skill and competition, or playful amusement
core_image: 绿茵场上一颗球被射向网窝，全场声音炸开
scene: 傍晚的球场灯刚亮起。The children played their favourite sport on the field until dark.
sceneCN: 这里 sport 是「体育运动」（第 1 个义项：有规则的体能竞技）；句意为孩子们在场上玩他们最爱的运动直到天黑。图中可辨识物件：足球场、球衣、夜灯。

pos.zh: 名词：运动；比赛；乐趣；突变型

derivatives.zh: 由动词现在分词作形容词，义为「运动的；公正的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「轻快运动型的」
复合词，义为「运动员；有运动家风度者」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「嬉戏的（书面）」

senses.title: A competitive physical game
senses.definition: an activity involving physical effort and skill, competed under rules
senses.definitionCN: 在规则下比拼体能与技巧的活动
senses.example: Swimming is a sport that suits every age.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳是一项适合所有年龄的运动。
senses.why: The field draws lines, and within the lines the body shows its best.
senses.whyCN: 场地画出界线，界线之内身体展现最佳。

senses.title: Amusement or fun
senses.definition: playful or lively amusement
senses.definitionCN: 轻快好玩的消遣
senses.example: The kittens made great sport of the yarn ball.
senses.exampleCN: 小猫们把毛线球玩得乐不可支。
senses.why: Before the stadium, sport meant any game the body enjoyed.
senses.whyCN: 在体育场之前，sport 泛指身体喜欢的任何游戏。

senses.title: Mockery or teasing
senses.definition: mocking or teasing treatment, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 取笑或戏弄，旧用法
senses.example: They made sport of his old-fashioned hat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拿他那顶老式帽子取乐。
senses.why: Fun can turn its edge outward and sting.
senses.whyCN: 玩闹可以翻出锋刃，变成刺痛。

senses.title: A plant or animal variant
senses.definition: an animal or plant that differs markedly from its kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类显著不同的动植物个体
senses.example: The gardener spotted a sport on the rose bush.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在玫瑰丛上发现一株变异枝。
senses.why: Life sometimes plays its own trick: one bud breaks the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 生命有时自娱：一个芽苞打破模式。

senses.title: To wear or show something showily
senses.definition: to wear or display something with pride or show
senses.definitionCN: 得意或张扬地穿戴、展示
senses.example: He sported a new leather jacket at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上炫耀新皮夹克。
senses.why: What is worn for joy is worn for eyes as well.
senses.whyCN: 为快乐而穿戴之物，也为目光而穿戴。

senses.title: To frolic or play
senses.definition: to play or move about in a lively way
senses.definitionCN: 轻快地玩耍或跳动
senses.example: Seals sported in the shallows at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时海豹在浅滩嬉戏。
senses.why: The game of the field returns to the wild water: play as nature's own.
senses.whyCN: 场上的游戏回到野水：玩耍是自然的本性。

senses.title: A good sport: fair and cheerful
senses.definition: a person who is fair, cheerful and uncomplaining in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 在困境中公正、开朗、不抱怨的人
senses.example: She lost the final but was a good sport about it.
senses.exampleCN: 她输了决赛却依然爽气大方。
senses.why: The rules of the game become rules of character.
senses.whyCN: 赛场的规则变成性格的规则。

senses.title: In sport: as a joke
senses.definition: not seriously, merely in play, in older phrasing
senses.definitionCN: 并非认真，仅为戏言，旧式说法
senses.example: He said it only in sport, and everyone laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是说着玩，大家都笑了。
senses.why: Words too can enter the field and leave the scoreboard empty.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能进场，只是不带记分牌。

intro.en: Sport is a shortened form of disport, the old word for carrying away in delight.
intro.cn: sport 是 disport 的截短形式，后者意为「被欢喜带离自身」。

items.en: *per- is generally reconstructed as "to lead, pass over"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *per- 表示「引领、度过」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin portare meant "to carry", giving the port- stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 portare 意为「搬运、携带」，给出 port- 词干。

items.en: Old French desport meant "pastime, pleasure", from desporter "to divert, carry away".
items.cn: 古法语 desport 意为「消遣、愉悦」，出自 desporter「使转移、带离」。

items.en: English took disport, and sport was clipped from it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先收 disport，十四世纪从中截出 sport。

items.en: The clipped word now rules stadiums, adjectives and even biology.
items.cn: 截短后的词如今统领体育场、形容词乃至生物学。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for play and competition.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收表示游戏与竞赛的词。

entries.definition: The plural, and the common attributive form as in sports bag.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，也常作定语如 sports bag。

entries.definition: An adjective for styles that look athletic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容运动风格的样式。

entries.definition: Relating to sport, or fair in attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 与运动相关，或指态度公正。

entries.definition: A place or a mark; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「地点；斑点」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: To hold up; ends alike but has another Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「支持」；结尾相近但拉丁词根不同。

entries.definition: A contest with rules; overlaps sport but can be mental.
entries.definitionCN: 有规则的竞赛，与 sport 重叠但可指智力游戏。

entries.definition: A pleasant way to pass time, without competition required.
entries.definitionCN: 消磨时光的乐事，不必竞技。

entries.definition: Track and field events, or physical training generally.
entries.definitionCN: 田径运动或体能训练。

entries.definition: Refreshing activity after work, broader than sport.
entries.definitionCN: 工作后恢复身心的活动，比 sport 更宽。

entries.definition: Simple enjoyment, matching the older amusement sense.
entries.definitionCN: 单纯的快乐，对应古老的玩闹义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the disport origin and the living idioms of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用 disport 词源与该词的常用习语。

normal.en: dis-port: carried away by delight; sport is that word clipped.
normal.cn: dis-port：被欢喜带走；sport 是它的截短。

normal.en: A good sport is someone who plays fair and laughs at loss.
normal.cn: good sport 是输得起、行得正的人。

normal.en: In sport means the words were only play, not promises.
normal.cn: in sport 表示话语只是游戏，并非承诺。

normal.en: Gardeners call a strange bud on a bush a sport: nature playing.
normal.cn: 园丁把灌木上的怪芽叫 sport：自然在玩耍。

normal.en: He sports a new jacket: he wears it so others see.
normal.cn: he sports a new jacket：穿戴招摇让人看见。

abstract.en: Draw the field first: lines make play into contest.
abstract.cn: 先画场地：界线把玩耍变成竞技。

abstract.en: Delight carries the body out of itself, the way the old word said.
abstract.cn: 欢喜把身体带离自身，如古词所言。

abstract.en: The bud that breaks the pattern is the field laughing at its own rules.
abstract.cn: 打破模式的芽苞，是场地在笑自己的规则。

examples.en: Football is the most watched sport in the world.
examples.cn: 足球是全世界观看人数最多的运动。

examples.en: The seals sported in the waves off the rocky point.
examples.cn: 海豹在礁岬外的浪中嬉戏。

examples.en: He sported a bright scarf all through the cold months.
examples.cn: 整个寒冬他都招摇地戴着一条亮色围巾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯波特」——被欢喜带离自身的一跃：运动；乐趣

root: sport 经古法语 desport「消遣」追溯至拉丁语 desportare「搬运开、使转移」，由 de-「离」加 portare「搬运」构成；一般认为印欧词根 *per- 表示「引领、度过」，更早来源不确定。disport 为未截短形式。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of sport run from the carried-away delight to the ruled field: play, mockery, mutation, and display.
sensesIntro.cn: sport 的义项从被带走的欢喜走到画了线的场地：游戏、嘲弄、变异与炫耀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a struck ball flying into the net as the lights come on.
core.cn: 核心意象：开灯时分，被击中的球飞入网窝。

branches.en: THE PLAY LINE: fun of body, fun of kittens, fun worn and fun wild.
branches.cn: 玩耍线：身体的乐、小猫的乐、穿戴的乐与野生的乐。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: lines and rules turn play into contest.
branches.cn: 场地线：界线与规则把玩耍变成竞技。

branches.en: THE OLD-EDGE LINE: fun that stings, and words said only in play.
branches.cn: 古锋线：会刺人的玩闹，与仅为戏言的话语。

branches.en: THE BUD LINE: a variant is nature playing its own game.
branches.cn: 芽苞线：变种是自然自娱的游戏。

branches.en: THE CHARACTER LINE: the rules of the field become rules of a fair heart.
branches.cn: 品格线：赛场的规则化作爽气的胸怀。

intro.en: Sport was clipped from disport, and English builds its own small family on the stub.
intro.cn: sport 由 disport 截短；英语在残干上建起自己的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare and Old French desport are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portare 与古法语 desport 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.example: The stem carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载整个词族。
它构成 disport 与 disportare。

items.example: The phrase turns field rules into character.
items.exampleCN: 该短语把赛场规则化为品格。

items.example: The phrase keeps the older amusement sense.
items.exampleCN: 该短语保留古老的玩闹义。

items.example: The phrase keeps the old teasing edge.
items.exampleCN: 该短语保留旧的打趣锋芒。

derivatives.zh: 由动词现在分词作形容词，义为「运动的；公正的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「轻快运动型的」
复合词，义为「运动员；有运动家风度者」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「嬉戏的（书面）」

definition_zh: 地点；斑点；发现；玷污；（名）现场；_spotlight 聚光
definition_en: a particular place, or a small round mark, or to notice something
core_image: 一盏舞台聚光灯在地板上打出一圈亮斑，光点正好落在主角脚下
scene: 剧场后台，场记板咔哒一响。The director spotted the young actor in the crowd of extras.
sceneCN: 这里 spot 是「发现、认出」（第 3 个义项：从人群中辨认出）；句意为导演在群众演员中发现了那位年轻演员。图中可辨识物件：场记板、聚光灯、人群。

pos.zh: 名词：地点；斑点；现场；聚光灯（the spot）

derivatives.zh: 复合词，义为「聚光灯；公众注目」
过去分词作形容词，义为「有斑点的」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「一尘不染的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「观察员；瞄准手」

senses.title: A particular place or location
senses.definition: a particular place or point on a surface or in an area
senses.definitionCN: 表面上或区域内的某个确定位置
senses.example: This is the exact spot where the old bridge stood.
senses.exampleCN: 这就是老桥当年所在的确切地点。
senses.why: A mark pins one place out of all others: the eye points where the dot sits.
senses.whyCN: 一个标记把某处从万处中钉出：眼睛指往圆点所在。

senses.title: A small round mark
senses.definition: a small round mark of a different colour
senses.definitionCN: 颜色不同的小圆点
senses.example: The leopard's coat is covered in dark spots.
senses.exampleCN: 豹的皮毛布满深色斑点。
senses.why: The dot is the smallest visible thing: everything larger is made of places.
senses.whyCN: 圆点是最小的可见物：更大的都由「位置」拼成。

senses.title: To notice or catch sight of
senses.definition: to notice someone or something, especially suddenly or with difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 注意到人或物，尤指突然或费劲地
senses.example: She spotted her old teacher across the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市场那头认出了老老师。
senses.why: The mark inside the eye: one detail stands out from the field.
senses.whyCN: 眼中的「斑点」：一个细节从背景里凸出来。

senses.title: To stain or dirty something
senses.definition: to mark or stain something with small patches
senses.definitionCN: 以小块污迹弄脏某物
senses.example: Coffee spotted the white tablecloth.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在白桌布上留下斑点。
senses.why: The dot falls where it will, and cleanliness is its victim.
senses.whyCN: 圆点随意落下，洁净成了受害者。

senses.title: On the spot: immediately or in trouble
senses.titleCN: on the spot：当场；为难境地
senses.definition: immediately, or in a difficult position requiring instant decision
senses.definitionCN: 立刻，或处于需即刻决断的困境
senses.example: The paramedics treated him on the spot.
senses.exampleCN: 急救员当场为他救治。
senses.why: The pointed place is where pressure lands: here and now.
senses.whyCN: 被钉住的点正是压力落处：就在此时此地。

senses.title: The spotlight and public attention
senses.definition: public attention or prominence, as in the spotlight
senses.definitionCN: 公众的注目，如聚光灯之下
senses.example: The scandal kept the minister in the spotlight.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻让部长一直处于聚光灯下。
senses.why: The stage mark of light picks one body for every eye.
senses.whyCN: 舞台上的光斑为每双眼睛挑出一个身影。

senses.title: A weak spot: a point of failure
senses.definition: a point where something or someone is vulnerable
senses.definitionCN: 事物或人易受攻击之处
senses.example: The plan's weak spot was its transport schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划的弱点在运输时间表。
senses.why: Where the dot sits, the surface can be pierced.
senses.whyCN: 圆点所在之处，表面可被穿透。

senses.title: A spot of: a small amount
senses.definition: a small amount of something, especially tea or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 少量某物，尤指茶或麻烦
senses.example: Let us have a spot of tea before we go.
senses.exampleCN: 走之前我们喝点茶吧。
senses.why: The dot shrinks the whole pot to a single mark of it.
senses.whyCN: 圆点把整壶缩成一个小小的标记。

intro.en: Spot is a native word of the mark and the dot, with a scattered family across the northern seas.
intro.cn: spot 是「标记与圆点」的本土词，词族散布在北方海域。

items.en: *spitt- is generally reconstructed as "to splash, speck"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spitt- 表示「溅上、斑点」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse spotti meant "a small spot or speck", the accepted near relative.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 spotti 意为「小斑点」，是公认的近亲。

items.en: Middle English spotte meant a stain or small mark, also a moral stain.
items.cn: 中古英语 spotte 指污渍或小点，也指道德污点。

items.en: The place sense grew from the marked point on a map or surface.
items.cn: 「地点」义由表面上被标记的点发展而来。

items.en: The word now serves maps, stains, eyes, spotlights and instant decisions.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词服务于地图、污渍、眼睛、聚光灯与当机立断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for marks and places.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收表示标记与地点的词。

entries.definition: A lamp that lights one area, or public attention.
entries.definitionCN: 聚光灯，或公众注目。

entries.definition: Covered in marks, as a spotted dog.
entries.definitionCN: 布满斑点，如斑点狗。

entries.definition: Completely clean, without a single mark.
entries.definitionCN: 一尘不染，毫无污点。

entries.definition: A quarrel or past of spit; letters shuffled and of different line.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「争吵」或 spit 的过去式；字母换位，词系不同。

entries.definition: Games and contests; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「运动」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: A general word for where something is.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「某物所在」的通用词。

entries.definition: A mark that sinks in and is hard to remove.
entries.definitionCN: 渗入且难除的污渍。

entries.definition: A very tiny spot or particle.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的斑点或微粒。

entries.definition: To become aware of something.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉到某物。

entries.definition: A spot of ink or a moral stain.
entries.definitionCN: 墨渍或道德污点。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dot image and the idioms the word really carries.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用圆点意象与该词的真实习语。

normal.en: A spot is a dot: a mark that also marks a place.
normal.cn: spot 是圆点：既作标记也标地点。

normal.en: On the spot means right there, right now.
normal.cn: on the spot 意为就在现场、就在此刻。

normal.en: Spot on means the answer hit the exact point.
normal.cn: spot on 表示答案正中靶点。

normal.en: Put on the spot is being pressed to answer at once.
normal.cn: put on the spot 是被当场逼问。

normal.en: A spot check samples a few random points.
normal.cn: spot check 从随机几个点抽样。

abstract.en: Picture the spotlight's circle on the floorboards: one bright dot among dark ones.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯在地板上的圆圈：暗色中的一点亮斑。

abstract.en: The eye is a hunter of dots: one fleck moving, and it is caught.
abstract.cn: 眼睛是圆点猎人：一点异动即被捕获。

abstract.en: Where the dot lands, the story happens: place and mark are one.
abstract.cn: 圆点落于何处，故事便发生何处：地点与标记合一。

examples.en: The hiker chose a shady spot for the lunch break.
examples.cn: 徒步者选了一处阴凉地点午餐歇脚。

examples.en: The doctor spotted the tiny rash behind the ear at once.
examples.cn: 医生立刻发现了耳后的细小皮疹。

examples.en: Rain spotted the window and blurred the street outside.
examples.cn: 雨点打上窗户，模糊了外面的街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯波特」——聚光圈钉住一点：地点；斑点；发现

root: spot 属日耳曼语源，一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spitt- 表示「溅上、斑点」，与古诺斯语 spotti「小斑点」相关，更早来源不确定。中古英语 spotte 兼指污渍与道德污点，「地点」义后起。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spot all circle one dot: the mark, the place it pins, the eye that finds it, and the stain that spoils.
sensesIntro.cn: spot 的义项都围绕一个圆点：标记、它钉住的地点、找到它的眼睛与弄脏它的污迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of spotlight on dark floorboards.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗色地板上聚光灯的一圈亮斑。

branches.en: THE MARK LINE: the dot on the map and the fleck on the coat.
branches.cn: 标记线：地图上的点与皮毛上的斑。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: one detail stands out and is caught.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：一个细节凸出并被捕获。

branches.en: THE STAIN LINE: where the dot falls, the surface can fail.
branches.cn: 污渍线：圆点落处，表面可破。

branches.en: THE HERE-AND-NOW LINE: decisions taken on the spot, troubles in small doses.
branches.cn: 此地此刻线：当场决断，麻烦按小份来。

branches.en: THE LIGHT LINE: the marked point becomes the stage's circle.
branches.cn: 光斑线：被标记的点化作舞台的圆。

intro.en: Spot is a bare Germanic root; compounds and suffixes gather around the dot.
intro.cn: spot 是裸的日耳曼词根；复合词与后缀围绕圆点聚集。

latinIntro.en: Spot is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: spot 属日耳曼语源，拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

The phrase pins time and place together.
items.exampleCN: 该短语把时间与地点钉在一起。

items.example: The phrase hits the marked point.
items.exampleCN: 该短语正中被标记的点。

definition_zh: 喷雾；喷洒；浪花；水沫；（名）喷剂；一簇（花）
definition_en: liquid sent in tiny drops through the air, or to scatter liquid in this way
core_image: 花园水管捏扁的管口喷出一片扇形水雾，雾里挂着一段彩虹
scene: 夏日的花园里水管嗡嗡作响。The gardener sprayed water over the dry flower beds.
sceneCN: 这里 spray 是「喷洒」（第 1 个义项：把液体散成细滴）；句意为园丁给干涸的花圃喷水。图中可辨识物件：水管、水雾、花圃、彩虹。

pos.zh: 名词：喷雾；浪花；喷剂；一小簇花
